title.raw: 卷五十六 志第三十二 禮十 Volume 56 Treatises 32: Rites 10

sentences.zh: 志第三十二 禮十

translations.literal: Treatises 32: Rites 10
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 32: Rites Ten

sentences.zh: （嘉禮四 賓禮）〉

translations.literal: (Auspicious Rites IV, Guest Rites)
translations.idiomatic: (Auspicious Rites IV: Guest Rites)

sentences.zh: 巡狩 東宮監國 皇長孫監國 頒詔儀 迎接詔赦儀 進書儀 進表箋儀鄉飲酒禮 蕃王朝貢禮 遣使之蕃國儀 蕃國遣使進表儀 品官相見禮 庶人相見禮

translations.literal: Imperial tours; Eastern Palace supervision of the state; imperial eldest grandson's supervision of the state; protocol for promulgating edicts; protocol for receiving edicts and amnesties; protocol for presenting books; protocol for presenting memorials and formal letters; village drinking ceremony; tributary audiences from foreign states; protocol for dispatching envoys to foreign states; protocol for foreign envoys presenting memorials; protocol for meetings between ranked officials; protocol for meetings among commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tours; crown prince as regent; imperial eldest grandson as regent; promulgation of edicts; receiving edicts and amnesties; presenting books; presenting memorials and formal letters; village drinking rite; tributary audiences; envoys to foreign states; foreign envoys presenting memorials; meetings between officials of rank; meetings among commoners.

sentences.zh: ○巡狩之制

translations.literal: Regulations for imperial tours.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations governing imperial tours.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年北巡，禮部行直省，凡有重事及四夷來朝與進表者，俱達行在所，小事達京師啓聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongle, on the northern tour, the Ministry of Rites notified the directly administered provinces that all weighty matters, audiences from the four quarters, and submitted memorials were to reach the traveling palace; minor matters were to reach the capital for reporting.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 6, during the northern tour, the Ministry of Rites instructed the directly governed provinces that important business, audiences from the four quarters, and memorial submissions were all to reach the mobile court, while minor matters were to be reported to the capital.

sentences.zh: 車駕將發，奏告天地、社稷、太廟、孝陵，祭大江、旗纛等神，軷祭於承天門。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to depart, memorials were presented to Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, the Grand Ancestral Temple, and the Xiaoling Mausoleum; sacrifices were offered to the Great River, banner streamers, and similar spirits; a shamans' exorcism sacrifice was performed at the Gate of Accepting Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor set out, reports were made to Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, the Grand Temple, and the Xiaoling tomb; offerings were made to the Great River, battle banners, and kindred deities, and an exorcistic shamans' sacrifice was performed at the Gate of Accepting Heaven.

sentences.zh: 緣途當祭者，遣官祭。

translations.literal: Where sacrifices were due along the route, officials were dispatched to perform them.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices required along the route were performed by dispatched officials.

sentences.zh: 將至北京，設壇祭北京山川等神。

translations.literal: As the emperor was about to reach Beijing, altars were set up to sacrifice to the mountains and rivers of Beijing and other spirits.
translations.idiomatic: On approaching Beijing, altars were erected for offerings to the capital's mountains, rivers, and other deities.

sentences.zh: 車駕至，奏告天地，祭境內山川。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage arrived, memorials were presented to Heaven and Earth, and sacrifices were offered to the mountains and rivers within the territory.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival, reports were made to Heaven and Earth, and offerings were presented to the mountains and rivers of the realm.

sentences.zh: 扈從馬步軍五萬。

translations.literal: The escort comprised fifty thousand cavalry and infantry.
translations.idiomatic: The escort numbered fifty thousand horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 侍從，五府都督各一，吏、戶、兵、刑四部堂上官各一，禮、工二部堂上官各二，都察院堂上官一，御史二十四，給事中十九，通政、大理、太常、光祿、鴻臚堂上官共二十，翰林院、內閣官三，侍講、修撰、典籍等官六，六部郎官共五十四，餘不具載。

translations.literal: In attendance: one commissioner-in-chief from each of the Five Chief Military Commissions; one chief minister each from the Ministries of Personnel, Revenue, War, and Justice; two chief ministers each from the Ministries of Rites and Works; one chief censor from the Censorate; twenty-four investigating censors; nineteen supervising secretaries; twenty chief ministers combined from the Offices of Transmission, Review, Imperial Sacrifices, Imperial Entertainments, and Ceremonial; three officials from the Hanlin Academy and the Grand Secretariat; six lecturing, compiling, and archival officials; fifty-four departmental directors from the six ministries—the remainder is not fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Those in attendance included one commissioner-in-chief from each of the Five Commissions; one chief minister each from Personnel, Revenue, War, and Justice; two each from Rites and Works; the Censorate's chief censor; twenty-four investigating censors; nineteen supervising secretaries; twenty chief ministers from Transmission, Review, Sacrifices, Entertainments, and Ceremonial combined; three from the Hanlin and Grand Secretariat; six lecturing, compiling, and archival officers; and fifty-four directors from the six ministries; the rest is not listed in full.

sentences.zh: 車駕將發，宴羣臣，賜扈從官及軍校鈔。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to depart, the emperor feasted the officials and bestowed paper money on the escorting officials and military officers.
translations.idiomatic: Before departure the emperor banqueted the officials and granted paper money to those in the escort and to the military officers.

sentences.zh: 至北京，宴羣臣、耆老，賜百官及命婦鈔。

translations.literal: On reaching Beijing, he feasted the officials and elders and bestowed paper money on all officials and titled ladies.
translations.idiomatic: At Beijing he entertained officials and elders and granted paper money to the entire bureaucracy and to titled ladies.

sentences.zh: 所過郡縣，官吏、生員、耆老朝見，分遣廷臣核守令賢否，即加黜陟。

translations.literal: In each commandery and county passed through, officials, students, and elders were received in audience; court ministers were dispatched separately to assess whether prefects and magistrates were worthy, and promotions or dismissals were made at once.
translations.idiomatic: At every commandery and county along the route, officials, students, and elders were received in audience; court ministers were sent out to judge the fitness of prefects and magistrates, who were promoted or dismissed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 給事、御史存問高年，賜幣帛酒肉。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries and censors inquired after the aged and bestowed silks, cloth, wine, and meat.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censors called on the elderly and gave them silks, cloth, wine, and meat.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十八年，幸承天。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiajing, the emperor visited Chengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 18 the emperor traveled to Chengtian.

sentences.zh: 先期親告上帝於玄極寶殿。

translations.literal: In advance he personally announced the matter to the Supreme Lord in the Hall of the Mysterious Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand he personally reported to the Supreme Lord in the Hall of the Mysterious Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 同日，告皇祖及睿宗廟，遣官分告北郊及成祖以下諸廟、社稷、日月、神祇。

translations.literal: On the same day he announced the matter at the temples of the imperial grandfather and Ruizong; officials were dispatched separately to announce at the northern suburban altar and at the temples from Chengzu downward, as well as at the altars of soil and grain, the sun and moon, and the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he reported at the temples of his imperial grandfather and Ruizong, while officials were sent to announce at the northern suburban altar, the temples from Chengzu onward, and the altars of soil and grain, sun and moon, and the spirits.

sentences.zh: 駕出正陽門，后妃輦轎從。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage departed through the Gate of Correct Yang; the empress and consorts followed in palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: The procession left by the Gate of Correct Yang, with the empress and consorts following in palanquins.

sentences.zh: 錦衣衛設欽制武陣駕，衛卒八千，奉輿輦，執儀仗。

translations.literal: The Brocade-Coated Guard established the imperially ordered martial formation escort; eight thousand guardsmen bore the carriages and palanquins and carried the ceremonial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: The Brocade-Coated Guard formed the imperial martial escort with eight thousand men to bear the carriages and palanquins and carry the ceremonial regalia.

sentences.zh: 衛指揮前驅。

translations.literal: The guard commanders rode in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Guard commanders rode ahead as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 武重臣二員留守，兵部尚書參贊機務，各賜敕行事。

translations.literal: Two senior military ministers remained on guard; the Minister of War assisted in state affairs, each granted an imperial commission to act.
translations.idiomatic: Two senior military ministers stayed behind to hold the capital, the Minister of War assisting in state affairs; each received an edict empowering him to act.

sentences.zh: 分命文武重臣，出督宣大、薊州、山海關，行九邊，亦各賜敕。

translations.literal: Senior civil and military ministers were appointed separately to supervise Xuanda, Jizhou, Shanhaiguan, and the tour of the nine border sectors, each likewise granted an imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: Senior civil and military ministers were dispatched to oversee Xuanda, Jizhou, Shanhaiguan, and the nine border sectors, each likewise receiving an edict of authority.

sentences.zh: 皇城及京城諸門，皆命文武大臣各一員坐守。

translations.literal: At every gate of the Imperial City and the capital, one civil or military grand minister was ordered to remain on guard.
translations.idiomatic: Each gate of the Imperial City and the capital was assigned one senior civil or military minister to hold the post.

sentences.zh: 設警備扈駕官軍六千。

translations.literal: Six thousand guard troops were posted for security and escort.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand troops were detailed for security and escort duty.

sentences.zh: 駕發，百官吉服送於彰義關外。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage set out, the officials in auspicious dress escorted him outside the Zhangyi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At departure the officials, in ceremonial dress, escorted the emperor beyond the Zhangyi Pass.

sentences.zh: 扈從官軍，略如永樂時數。

translations.literal: The escorting officials and troops were roughly the same in number as in the Yongle period.
translations.idiomatic: The escort was roughly the same size as in the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 先發在途者免朝參，惟禮兵二部、鴻臚、太常、科道糾儀官及光祿寺從行。

translations.literal: Those who had set out earlier on the route were excused from court attendance; only the Ministries of Rites and War, the Ceremonial, Sacrifices, censorial and supervising secretaries charged with ritual correction, and the Imperial Entertainments accompanied the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Officials already on the road were excused from daily audience; only Rites and War, Ceremonial, Sacrifices, censorial and supervising officers for ritual discipline, and Imperial Entertainments traveled with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 過真定，望祭北嶽。

translations.literal: Passing Zhending, he performed a distant-offering sacrifice to the Northern Marchmount.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhending he offered a distant sacrifice to the Northern Marchmount.

sentences.zh: 帝常服，從臣大臣及巡撫都御史吉服行禮。

translations.literal: The emperor wore ordinary dress; the accompanying grand ministers and the grand coordinators and censors-in-chief wore auspicious dress to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore ordinary dress, while accompanying grand ministers and the regional grand coordinators and censors-in-chief wore ceremonial dress to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 衛輝，遣官祭濟瀆。

translations.literal: At Weihui, officials were dispatched to sacrifice to the Ji River.
translations.idiomatic: At Weihui officials were sent to sacrifice to the Ji River.

sentences.zh: 鈞州，望祭中嶽；

translations.literal: At Junzhou, a distant-offering sacrifice to the Central Marchmount;
translations.idiomatic: At Junzhou, a distant sacrifice to the Central Marchmount;

sentences.zh: 滎澤，祭河，禮如北嶽。

translations.literal: at Rong Marsh, sacrifice to the River, the rites being the same as for the Northern Marchmount.
translations.idiomatic: at Rong Marsh, sacrifice to the River with rites like those for the Northern Marchmount.

sentences.zh: 南陽，遣祭武當山。

translations.literal: At Nanyang, sacrifice was dispatched to Mount Wudang.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanyang officials were sent to sacrifice at Mount Wudang.

sentences.zh: 途次古帝王、聖賢、忠臣、烈士祠墓，遣官致祭。

translations.literal: Along the route, at shrines and tombs of ancient emperors and kings, sages, loyal ministers, and martyrs, officials were dispatched to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At shrines and tombs of ancient rulers, sages, loyal ministers, and martyrs along the route, officials were sent to make offerings.

sentences.zh: 撫、按、三司迎於境上，至行宮，吉服朝見。

translations.literal: Grand coordinators, surveillance commissioners, and the three provincial offices welcomed him at the border; at the traveling palace they were received in audience in auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinators, surveillance commissioners, and the three provincial offices met him at the border; at the traveling palace they were received in audience in ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 生員耆老，俱三十里外迎。

translations.literal: Students and elders alike welcomed him thirty li outside.
translations.idiomatic: Students and elders alike welcomed him from thirty li out.

sentences.zh: 所過王府，親王常服候駕，隨至行宮，冕服朝見。

translations.literal: At each princely residence passed through, the prince in ordinary dress awaited the imperial carriage, then followed to the traveling palace and was received in audience in full ceremonial robes.
translations.idiomatic: At each princely residence the prince, in ordinary dress, awaited the emperor, followed to the traveling palace, and was received in full court regalia.

sentences.zh: 賜宴，宗室不許出。

translations.literal: A banquet was granted; members of the imperial clan were not permitted to leave.
translations.idiomatic: He granted a banquet; members of the imperial clan were not allowed to leave.

sentences.zh: 至承天，詣獻皇帝廟謁告。

translations.literal: On reaching Chengtian, he went to the temple of the Xian Emperor to announce his arrival.
translations.idiomatic: At Chengtian he went to the temple of the Xian Emperor to report his arrival.

sentences.zh: 越四日，行告天禮於龍飛殿丹陛上，奉獻皇帝配。

translations.literal: Four days later, he performed the announcement-to-Heaven rite on the vermillion steps of the Dragon Ascent Hall, with the Xian Emperor as associate.
translations.idiomatic: Four days later he performed the announcement to Heaven on the vermillion steps of the Dragon Ascent Hall, with the Xian Emperor as associate.

sentences.zh: 更皮弁服，詣國社稷及山川壇行禮，次日，謁顯陵。

translations.literal: He changed into the leather cap and performed rites at the altars of the state's soil and grain and of mountains and rivers; the next day he visited the Xian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Changing into the leather cap, he performed rites at the altars of soil and grain and of mountains and rivers; the next day he visited the Xian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 次日，從駕官上表賀，遂頒詔如儀。

translations.literal: The next day, the officials in the escort submitted congratulatory memorials, and an edict was then promulgated according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The following day the escorting officials submitted congratulatory memorials, and an edict was promulgated as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 回京，親謝上帝、皇祖、皇考，分遣官告郊、廟、社稷、羣神，行禮如初。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital, he personally gave thanks to the Supreme Lord, the imperial grandfather, and the imperial father; officials were dispatched separately to announce at the suburban altars, temples, altars of soil and grain, and the host of spirits, performing the rites as at the outset.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he personally gave thanks to the Supreme Lord, his imperial grandfather, and his imperial father, while officials were again sent to announce at the suburban altars, temples, altars of soil and grain, and the spirits, performing the rites as before.

sentences.zh: ○東宮監國

translations.literal: Eastern Palace supervision of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince as regent.

sentences.zh: 古制，太子出曰：「撫軍」，守曰：「監國」。

translations.literal: In ancient regulations, when the heir apparent went forth it was called "pacifying the army"; when he remained behind it was called "supervising the state."
translations.idiomatic: Under the ancient regulations, when the heir apparent went out it was termed "pacifying the army," and when he remained it was termed "supervising the state."

sentences.zh: 三代而下，惟唐太子監國結雙龍符，而其儀不著。

translations.literal: From the Three Dynasties downward, only the Tang heir apparent, when supervising the state, bound the paired dragon tallies, yet the ritual is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Dynasties, only the Tang heir apparent, when acting as regent, bound the paired dragon tallies, but the ceremony itself is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年，駕幸北京，定制，凡常朝，皇太子於午門左視事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongle, when the imperial carriage visited Beijing, regulations were fixed: for ordinary court sessions the crown prince conducted affairs to the left of the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 7, when the emperor went to Beijing, regulations were set: for regular audiences the crown prince handled affairs to the left of the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 左右侍衛及各官啓事如常儀。

translations.literal: The left and right guards and all officials reported business according to the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right guards and all officials reported business in the usual manner.

sentences.zh: 若御文華殿，承旨召入者方入。

translations.literal: If the emperor was at the Literary Splendor Hall, only those summoned by imperial command might enter.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor was at the Literary Splendor Hall, only those summoned by edict might enter.

sentences.zh: 凡內外軍機及王府急務，悉奏請。

translations.literal: All internal and external military affairs and urgent business of princely establishments were to be memorialized for decision.
translations.idiomatic: All military affairs within and without and urgent princely business were to be submitted for decision.

sentences.zh: 有邊警，即調軍剿捕，仍馳奏行在。

translations.literal: If there was a border alarm, troops were at once mobilized to suppress and capture, while a rapid memorial was still sent to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: On a border alarm troops were immediately dispatched to suppress it, while a rapid report was still sent to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 皇城及各門守衛，皆增置官軍。

translations.literal: Guards at the Imperial City and at every gate were all reinforced with additional officials and troops.
translations.idiomatic: Guards at the Imperial City and at every gate were all reinforced.

sentences.zh: 遇聖節、正旦、冬至，皇太子率百官於文華殿前拜表，行十二拜禮。

translations.literal: On the emperor's birthday, New Year's Day, and the winter solstice, the crown prince led the officials in presenting a memorial before the Literary Splendor Hall, performing the twelve-prostration rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's birthday, New Year's Day, and the winter solstice, the crown prince led the officials in presenting a memorial before the Literary Splendor Hall with twelve prostrations.

sentences.zh: 表由中門出，皇太子由左門送至午門，還宮。

translations.literal: The memorial went out through the central gate; the crown prince escorted it through the left gate to the Meridian Gate, then returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial left by the central gate; the crown prince escorted it through the left gate to the Meridian Gate and then returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 百官導至長安右門外，文五品、武四品以上，及近侍官、監察御史，俱乘馬導三山門外，以表授進奏官。

translations.literal: The officials escorted it to outside the Chang'an Right Gate; civil officials of the fifth rank and above, military of the fourth rank and above, intimate attendants, and investigating censors all rode on horseback to escort it outside the Three Mountain Gate and hand the memorial to the memorial-presenting officer.
translations.idiomatic: The officials escorted it to beyond the Chang'an Right Gate; civil officials of fifth rank and above, military of fourth rank and above, intimate attendants, and investigating censors all rode out to the Three Mountain Gate and handed the memorial to the presenting officer.

sentences.zh: 至期，告天祝壽，行八拜禮。

translations.literal: When the day arrived, Heaven was announced to and longevity wished, with the eight-prostration rite performed.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day Heaven was announced to and longevity wished, with eight prostrations.

sentences.zh: 其正旦、冬至、千秋節，百官於文華殿慶賀如常儀。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and the Thousand Autumns Festival, the officials offered congratulations at the Literary Splendor Hall according to the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and the Thousand Autumns Festival, officials offered congratulations at the Literary Splendor Hall as usual.

sentences.zh: 凡享太廟及社稷諸神之祭，先期敕皇太子攝祭。

translations.literal: For all sacrifices at the Grand Temple and to the spirits of soil and grain, the crown prince was beforehand commanded to perform the sacrifice by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: For all sacrifices at the Grand Temple and to the altars of soil and grain, the crown prince was beforehand ordered to officiate by proxy.

sentences.zh: 其祀典神祇，太常寺於行在奏聞，遣官行禮。

translations.literal: For spirits in the canonical sacrificial register, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported to the traveling palace and dispatched officials to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: For spirits in the canonical register, the Court of Sacrifices reported to the mobile court and dispatched officials to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 凡四夷來朝，循例賜宴，命禮部遣送行在所。

translations.literal: For all audiences from the four quarters, banquets were granted according to precedent, and the Ministry of Rites was ordered to escort them to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: For audiences from the four quarters, banquets were granted as usual and the Ministry of Rites was ordered to escort the envoys to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 凡詔書至，設龍亭儀仗大樂，百官朝服，出三山門外奉迎。

translations.literal: Whenever an imperial edict arrived, the dragon pavilion, guard of honor, and grand music were set up; the officials in court dress went out beyond the Three Mountain Gate to welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an imperial edict arrived, the dragon pavilion, guard of honor, and grand music were set up, and officials in court dress went out beyond the Three Mountain Gate to receive it.

sentences.zh: 皇太子冕服迎於午門前，至文華殿，行五拜三叩頭禮，升殿展讀。

translations.literal: The crown prince in full ceremonial robes welcomed it before the Meridian Gate; at the Literary Splendor Hall he performed five prostrations and three kowtows, ascended the hall, and unrolled and read it.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, in full court regalia, received it before the Meridian Gate; at the Literary Splendor Hall he made five prostrations and three kowtows, ascended the hall, and read it aloud.

sentences.zh: 使者捧詔置龍亭中，皇太子送至午門外。

translations.literal: The envoy bore the edict and placed it in the dragon pavilion; the crown prince escorted it to outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy placed the edict in the dragon pavilion; the crown prince escorted it to beyond the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 禮部官置詔書雲輿中，文武二品以上官迎至承天門，開讀如儀。

translations.literal: A Ministry of Rites official placed the edict in the cloud carriage; civil and military officials of the second rank and above escorted it to the Gate of Accepting Heaven, where it was opened and read according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: A Ministry of Rites officer placed the edict in the cloud carriage; civil and military officials of second rank and above escorted it to the Gate of Accepting Heaven, where it was opened and read as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 以鼓樂送使者詣會同館。

translations.literal: With drums and music the envoy was escorted to the Hall of Joint Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Drums and music escorted the envoy to the Hall of Joint Harmony.

sentences.zh: 使者見皇太子，行四拜禮，賜宴於禮部。

translations.literal: The envoy was received by the crown prince and performed four prostrations; a banquet was granted at the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was received by the crown prince and made four prostrations; a banquet was given at the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十二年北征，復定制。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, on the northern campaign, regulations were again fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, on the northern campaign, regulations were revised again.

sentences.zh: 常朝於文華殿視事，文武啓事，俱達北京。

translations.literal: For ordinary court sessions affairs were conducted at the Literary Splendor Hall; civil and military reports all reached Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: Regular audiences were held at the Literary Splendor Hall, and civil and military reports all went to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十八年南巡，命皇太子監國。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiajing, on the southern tour, the crown prince was ordered to supervise the state.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 18, on the southern tour, the crown prince was ordered to act as regent.

sentences.zh: 時太子幼，命輔臣一人居守，軍國機務悉聽啓行。

translations.literal: As the heir apparent was young, one assisting minister was ordered to remain on guard; all military and state affairs were to be decided on memorial and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Because the heir was young, one assisting minister was left in charge; all military and civil affairs were to be decided on memorial and executed.

sentences.zh: ○皇太孫監國

translations.literal: Imperial eldest grandson's supervision of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial eldest grandson as regent.

sentences.zh: 永樂八年，帝自北京北征。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongle, the emperor from Beijing launched the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 8 the emperor marched north from Beijing.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子已監國於南，乃命皇長孫居北京監國。

translations.literal: As the crown prince was already supervising the state in the south, the imperial eldest grandson was ordered to remain at Beijing and supervise the state.
translations.idiomatic: Because the crown prince was already regent in the south, the imperial eldest grandson was ordered to remain at Beijing as regent.

sentences.zh: 時宣宗未冠，及冠始加稱皇太孫云。

translations.literal: At the time the Xuanzong Emperor had not yet come of age; only after he reached majority was the title imperial eldest grandson added, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the future Xuanzong Emperor had not yet come of age; only after his capping was he styled imperial eldest grandson.

sentences.zh: 其制，每日皇長孫於奉天門左視事，侍衛如常儀。

translations.literal: Under this system, each day the imperial eldest grandson conducted affairs to the left of the Gate of Accepting Heaven, with guards as in the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Under this arrangement the imperial eldest grandson handled affairs daily to the left of the Gate of Accepting Heaven, with guards as usual.

sentences.zh: 諸司有事，具啓施行。

translations.literal: When any office had business, it was fully reported and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When any office had business, it was reported in full and executed.

sentences.zh: 若軍機及王府要務，一啓皇太子處分，一奏聞行在所。

translations.literal: For military affairs and urgent princely business, one report went to the crown prince for disposition and one memorial was sent to announce the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: For military affairs and urgent princely business, one report went to the crown prince for decision and one memorial was sent to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 聖節，設香案於奉天殿，行禮如常儀。

translations.literal: On the emperor's birthday, an incense table was set up in the Hall of Accepting Heaven and rites were performed as in the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's birthday an incense table was set up in the Hall of Accepting Heaven and rites were performed as usual.

sentences.zh: 天下諸司表文俱詣北京。

translations.literal: Memorials from all offices under Heaven were all sent to Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from all offices throughout the realm were sent to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 四夷朝貢俱送南京，武選及官民有犯，大者啓皇太子，小者皇長孫行之。

translations.literal: Tributary missions from the four quarters were all sent to Nanjing; for military selection and offenses by officials and commoners, major cases were reported to the crown prince and minor ones were handled by the imperial eldest grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Tributary missions from the four quarters were sent to Nanjing; for military appointments and offenses by officials and commoners, major cases went to the crown prince and minor ones were handled by the imperial eldest grandson.

sentences.zh: 皇親有犯，啓皇太子所。

translations.literal: If an imperial kinsman committed an offense, the matter was reported to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: If an imperial kinsman offended, the matter was reported to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 犯情重及謀逆者，即時拘執，命皇親會問。

translations.literal: In cases of grave offense or plotting rebellion, the culprit was at once detained and imperial kinsmen were ordered to conduct a joint inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: In cases of grave offense or treason the culprit was immediately detained and imperial kinsmen were ordered to conduct a joint inquiry.

sentences.zh: 不服，乃命公、侯、伯、五府、六部、都察院、大理寺會皇親再問，啓皇太子，候車駕回京，奏請處分。

translations.literal: If he did not submit, dukes, marquises, earls, the Five Commissions, six ministries, Censorate, and Court of Review were then ordered to join the imperial kinsmen in a second inquiry, report to the crown prince, and await the imperial carriage's return to the capital before memorializing for disposition.
translations.idiomatic: If he did not submit, dukes, marquises, earls, the Five Commissions, six ministries, Censorate, and Court of Review joined the imperial kinsmen in a second inquiry, reported to the crown prince, and awaited the emperor's return before memorializing for disposition.

sentences.zh: ○頒詔儀

translations.literal: Protocol for promulgating edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Promulgation of edicts.

sentences.zh: 凡頒命四方，有詔書，有赦書、有敕符、丹符，有制諭、手詔。

translations.literal: Whenever commands were issued to the four quarters, there were edict documents, amnesty documents, commission tallies and vermilion tallies, and regulatory pronouncements and handwritten edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Commands issued to the four quarters took the form of edicts, amnesties, commission tallies and vermilion tallies, regulatory pronouncements, and handwritten edicts.

sentences.zh: 詔赦，先於闕廷宣讀，然後頒行。

translations.literal: Edicts and amnesties were first proclaimed and read at the palace court, then promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts and amnesties were first read aloud at the palace court, then promulgated.

sentences.zh: 敕符等，則使者齎付所授官，祕不敢發。

translations.literal: Commission tallies and the like were borne by envoys and delivered to the appointed official, who kept them secret and dared not open them.
translations.idiomatic: Commission tallies and the like were delivered by envoys to the appointed official, who kept them sealed and dared not open them.

sentences.zh: 開讀迎接，儀各不同。

translations.literal: The protocols for opening, reading, and receiving them each differed.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonies for opening, reading, and receiving them differed in each case.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年，定頒詔儀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu, the protocol for promulgating edicts was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 26 the protocol for promulgating edicts was established.

sentences.zh: 設御座於奉天殿，設寶案於殿東，陳中和韶樂於殿內，設大樂於午門及承天門外，設宣讀案於承天門上，西南向。

translations.literal: The imperial throne was set up in the Hall of Accepting Heaven; the seal table was set up on the east side of the hall; Central Harmony music was arrayed inside the hall; grand music was set up outside the Meridian Gate and the Gate of Accepting Heaven; the proclamation table was set on the Gate of Accepting Heaven, facing southwest.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial throne was set up in the Hall of Accepting Heaven; the seal table on the hall's east side; Central Harmony music inside the hall; grand music outside the Meridian Gate and the Gate of Accepting Heaven; and the proclamation table on the Gate of Accepting Heaven, facing southwest.

sentences.zh: 清晨，校尉擎雲蓋於殿內簾前，百官朝服班承天門外，公侯班午門外，東西向。

translations.literal: At dawn, guards bore the cloud canopy before the curtain inside the hall; the officials in court dress lined up outside the Gate of Accepting Heaven; dukes and marquises lined up outside the Meridian Gate, facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn guards bore the cloud canopy before the hall curtain; officials in court dress lined up outside the Gate of Accepting Heaven; dukes and marquises lined up outside the Meridian Gate, facing east and west.

sentences.zh: 皇帝皮弁服，升殿如儀。

translations.literal: The emperor in the leather cap ascended the hall according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, in the leather cap, ascended the hall as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 禮部官捧詔書詣案前，用寶訖，置雲蓋中。

translations.literal: A Ministry of Rites official bore the edict to the table; after the seal was applied, it was placed in the cloud canopy.
translations.idiomatic: A Ministry of Rites officer carried the edict to the table; after the seal was applied, it was placed in the cloud canopy.

sentences.zh: 校尉擎雲蓋，由殿東門出。

translations.literal: Guards bore the cloud canopy and went out through the hall's east gate.
translations.idiomatic: Guards bore the cloud canopy out through the hall's east gate.

sentences.zh: 大樂作，自東陛降，由奉天門至金水橋南午門外，樂作，公侯前導，迎至承天門上。

translations.literal: Grand music sounded; they descended the eastern steps, passed from the Gate of Accepting Heaven to south of the Golden Water Bridge outside the Meridian Gate; music sounded; dukes and marquises led in advance and escorted it up to the Gate of Accepting Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Grand music played as they descended the eastern steps, passed from the Gate of Accepting Heaven to south of the Golden Water Bridge outside the Meridian Gate, with dukes and marquises leading the escort up to the Gate of Accepting Heaven.

sentences.zh: 鳴贊唱排班，文武官就位，樂作。

translations.literal: The herald sang the call to form ranks; civil and military officials took their places; music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: The herald called ranks to form; civil and military officials took their places; music played.

sentences.zh: 四拜，樂止。

translations.literal: Four prostrations; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Four prostrations were made; music ceased.

sentences.zh: 宣讀展讀官升案，稱有制，衆官跪。

translations.literal: The proclamation and unrolling officers ascended the table, announced that there was an imperial command, and all officials knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The proclamation and reading officers ascended the table, announced that there was an imperial command, and all officials knelt.

sentences.zh: 禮部官捧詔書，授宣讀官。

translations.literal: A Ministry of Rites official bore the edict and handed it to the proclamation officer.
translations.idiomatic: A Ministry of Rites officer carried the edict and handed it to the proclamation officer.

sentences.zh: 宣訖，禮部官捧置雲蓋中。

translations.literal: When the proclamation was finished, a Ministry of Rites official bore it and placed it in the cloud canopy.
translations.idiomatic: After the proclamation, a Ministry of Rites officer placed it back in the cloud canopy.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱俯伏興，樂作。

translations.literal: The ritual herald sang "prostrate and rise"; music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual herald called "prostrate and rise"; music played.

sentences.zh: 四拜，樂止。

translations.literal: Four prostrations; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Four prostrations were made; music ceased.

sentences.zh: 舞蹈山呼，又四拜。

translations.literal: They danced and shouted the mountain call, then performed four prostrations again.
translations.idiomatic: They danced and shouted the mountain call, then made four more prostrations.

sentences.zh: 儀禮司奏禮畢，駕興。

translations.literal: The Office of Ceremonial reported that the rites were complete, and the imperial carriage rose.
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Ceremonial announced that the rites were complete, and the emperor departed.

sentences.zh: 禮部官捧詔書分授使者，百官退。

translations.literal: Ministry of Rites officials bore the edicts and distributed them to the envoys; the officials withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Rites officers distributed the edicts to the envoys, and the officials withdrew.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年續定，鴻臚官設詔案，錦衣衛設雲蓋盤於奉天殿內東，別設雲盤於承天門上。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiajing it was revised: Ceremonial officials set up the edict table; the Brocade-Coated Guard set up the cloud-canopy tray on the east side inside the Hall of Accepting Heaven, and a separate cloud tray was set on the Gate of Accepting Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 6 the protocol was revised: Ceremonial officials set up the edict table; the Brocade-Coated Guard placed the cloud-canopy tray on the east side inside the Hall of Accepting Heaven, with a separate cloud tray on the Gate of Accepting Heaven.

sentences.zh: 設彩輿於午門外，鴻臚官設宣讀案於承天門上。

translations.literal: A ceremonial carriage was set up outside the Meridian Gate; Ceremonial officials set up the proclamation table on the Gate of Accepting Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: A ceremonial carriage was placed outside the Meridian Gate, and Ceremonial officials set up the proclamation table on the Gate of Accepting Heaven.

sentences.zh: 百官入丹墀侍立，帝冕服升座，如朝儀。

translations.literal: The officials entered the vermillion courtyard and stood in attendance; the emperor in full ceremonial robes ascended the throne as at a court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Officials entered the vermillion courtyard and stood in attendance; the emperor, in full court regalia, took the throne as at a regular audience.

sentences.zh: 翰林院官捧詔書從，至御座前東立。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academy officials bore the edict in attendance and stood on the east before the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin officials carried the edict in attendance and stood to the east before the throne.

sentences.zh: 百官入班，四拜，出至承天門外。

translations.literal: The officials entered their ranks, performed four prostrations, and went out to outside the Gate of Accepting Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The officials formed ranks, made four prostrations, and went out beyond the Gate of Accepting Heaven.

sentences.zh: 贊頒詔，翰林院官捧詔書授禮部官，捧至雲盤案上。

translations.literal: The herald called for the promulgation of the edict; Hanlin officials bore the edict and handed it to Ministry of Rites officials, who bore it to the cloud-tray table.
translations.idiomatic: The herald called for promulgation; Hanlin officials handed the edict to Ministry of Rites officers, who carried it to the cloud-tray table.

sentences.zh: 校尉擎雲蓋，俱從殿左門出，至午門外，捧詔置彩輿內。

translations.literal: Guards bore the cloud canopy, all going out through the hall's left gate to outside the Meridian Gate, where they bore the edict and placed it in the ceremonial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Guards bore the cloud canopy out through the hall's left gate to beyond the Meridian Gate and placed the edict in the ceremonial carriage.

sentences.zh: 公侯伯三品以上官前導，迎至承天門上，宣讀贊拜，俱如上儀。

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, earls, and officials of the third rank and above led in advance and escorted it up to the Gate of Accepting Heaven; proclamation, reading, and prostration were all as in the protocol above.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, marquises, earls, and officials of third rank and above led the escort up to the Gate of Accepting Heaven; proclamation, reading, and prostrations followed the protocol above.

sentences.zh: 禮部官捧詔書授錦衣衛官，置雲匣中，以彩索系之龍竿，頒降。

translations.literal: Ministry of Rites officials bore the edict and handed it to Brocade-Coated Guard officials, who placed it in the cloud casket, tied it with colored cord to the dragon pole, and promulgated it downward.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Rites officers handed the edict to Brocade-Coated Guard officers, who placed it in the cloud casket, tied it with colored cord to the dragon pole, and lowered it for promulgation.

sentences.zh: 禮部官捧置龍亭內，鼓樂迎至禮部，授使者頒行。

translations.literal: Ministry of Rites officials bore it and placed it in the dragon pavilion; with drums and music it was escorted to the Ministry of Rites and handed to envoys for promulgation.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Rites officers placed it in the dragon pavilion; drums and music escorted it to the Ministry of Rites, where it was handed to envoys for distribution.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年，詔出至皇極門，即奏禮畢，駕還。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Longqing, once the edict had been taken out to the Gate of Supreme Ultimate, it was at once reported that the rites were complete and the imperial carriage returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 6, once the edict reached the Gate of Supreme Ultimate, the rites were declared complete and the emperor returned.

sentences.zh: ○迎接詔赦儀

translations.literal: Protocol for receiving edicts and amnesties.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving edicts and amnesties.

sentences.zh: 洪武中定。

translations.literal: Fixed in the Hongwu reign.
translations.idiomatic: Established in the Hongwu reign.

sentences.zh: 凡遣使開讀詔赦，本處官具龍亭儀仗鼓樂，出郭迎。

translations.literal: Whenever envoys were dispatched to open and read edicts and amnesties, local officials prepared the dragon pavilion, guard of honor, and drums and music, and went outside the city wall to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever envoys arrived to open and read edicts and amnesties, local officials prepared the dragon pavilion, guard of honor, and music and went outside the walls to receive them.

sentences.zh: 使者下馬，奉詔書置龍亭中，南向，本處官朝服行五拜禮。

translations.literal: The envoy dismounted, bore the edict and placed it in the dragon pavilion facing south; local officials in court dress performed five prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy dismounted, placed the edict in the dragon pavilion facing south, and local officials in court dress made five prostrations.

sentences.zh: 衆官及鼓樂前導，使者上馬隨龍亭後，至公廨門。

translations.literal: The officials and drums and music led in advance; the envoy mounted and followed behind the dragon pavilion to the gate of the government compound.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and music led the way; the envoy mounted and followed the dragon pavilion to the government compound gate.

sentences.zh: 衆官先入，文武東西序立，候龍亭至，排班四拜。

translations.literal: The officials entered first; civil and military officials stood in order east and west; when the dragon pavilion arrived they formed ranks and performed four prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: Officials entered first; civil and military officials stood in order to east and west; when the dragon pavilion arrived they formed ranks and made four prostrations.

sentences.zh: 使者捧詔授展讀官，展讀官跪受，詣開讀案。

translations.literal: The envoy bore the edict and handed it to the unrolling officer; the unrolling officer knelt to receive it and went to the reading table.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy handed the edict to the unrolling officer, who knelt to receive it and went to the reading table.

sentences.zh: 宣讀訖，捧詔授朝使，仍置龍亭中。

translations.literal: When the proclamation and reading were finished, he bore the edict and handed it to the court envoy, who again placed it in the dragon pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After the proclamation and reading, he handed the edict to the court envoy, who placed it back in the dragon pavilion.

sentences.zh: 衆官四拜，舞蹈山呼，復四拜畢。

translations.literal: The officials performed four prostrations, danced and shouted the mountain call, and again performed four prostrations to completion.
translations.idiomatic: The officials made four prostrations, danced and shouted the mountain call, and made four more prostrations to conclude.

sentences.zh: 班首詣龍亭前，跪問皇躬萬福，使者鞠躬答曰：「聖躬萬福。

translations.literal: The rank leader went before the dragon pavilion, knelt, and inquired after the emperor's myriad blessings; the envoy bowed and answered: "The sacred person enjoys myriad blessings."
translations.idiomatic: The rank leader went before the dragon pavilion, knelt, and inquired after the emperor's health; the envoy bowed and answered: "His Majesty enjoys myriad blessings."

sentences.zh: 」衆官退，易服見使者，並行兩拜禮。

translations.literal: " The officials withdrew, changed dress, and received the envoy, each performing two prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: " The officials withdrew, changed dress, received the envoy, and each made two prostrations.

sentences.zh: 復具鼓樂送詔於官亭。

translations.literal: Again they prepared drums and music and escorted the edict to the official pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Again they prepared drums and music and escorted the edict to the official rest pavilion.

sentences.zh: 如有出使官在，則先守臣行禮。

translations.literal: If a dispatched official was present, the local defending official performed the rites first.
translations.idiomatic: If a dispatched official was present, the local defending official performed the rites first.

sentences.zh: ○進書儀

translations.literal: Protocol for presenting books.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting books.

sentences.zh: 進書儀惟《實錄》最重。

translations.literal: Among protocols for presenting books, that for the Veritable Records was weightiest.
translations.idiomatic: Of all protocols for presenting books, that for the Veritable Records was the most important.

sentences.zh: 皇帝具袞冕，百官朝服，進表稱賀。

translations.literal: The emperor wore full ceremonial robes; the officials wore court dress; a memorial was presented offering congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore full ceremonial robes, officials wore court dress, and a congratulatory memorial was presented.

sentences.zh: 其餘纂修書成，則以表進。

translations.literal: When other compiled works were completed, they were presented by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When other compiled works were completed, they were presented by memorial.

sentences.zh: 重錄書及玉牒，止捧進。

translations.literal: For recopied books and the jade genealogy, presentation by bearing alone sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: For recopied books and the jade genealogy, presentation by bearing alone sufficed.

sentences.zh: 茲詳載進《實錄》儀，餘可推見云。

translations.literal: Here the protocol for presenting the Veritable Records is recorded in detail; the rest may be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: Here the protocol for presenting the Veritable Records is recorded in detail; the rest may be inferred.

sentences.zh: 建文時，《太祖實錄》成，其進儀無考。

translations.literal: In the Jianwen reign, when the Veritable Records of Taizu were completed, the presentation protocol cannot be verified.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwen reign, when the Veritable Records of Taizu were completed, the presentation protocol is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，重修《太祖實錄》成。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, the revised Veritable Records of Taizu were completed.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 the revised Veritable Records of Taizu were completed.

sentences.zh: 設香案於奉天殿丹陛正中，表案于丹陛之東，設寶輿於奉天門，設鹵簿大樂如儀。

translations.literal: An incense table was set at the center of the vermillion steps of the Hall of Accepting Heaven, a memorial table on the east of the steps, a treasure carriage at the Gate of Accepting Heaven, and ceremonial guard and grand music as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: An incense table was placed at the center of the vermillion steps of the Hall of Accepting Heaven, a memorial table to the east, a treasure carriage at the Gate of Accepting Heaven, and ceremonial guard and grand music as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 史官捧《實錄》置輿中，帝御殿如大朝儀。

translations.literal: Historiographers bore the Veritable Records and placed them in the carriage; the emperor attended the hall as at a grand court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Historiographers placed the Veritable Records in the carriage; the emperor took the hall as at a grand audience.

sentences.zh: 百官詣丹墀左右立，鴻臚官引寶輿至丹陛上，史官舉《實錄》置於案，遂入班。

translations.literal: The officials went to stand left and right in the vermillion courtyard; Ceremonial officials led the treasure carriage to the vermillion steps; historiographers lifted the Veritable Records and placed them on the table, then entered the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Officials stood to left and right in the vermillion courtyard; Ceremonial officials led the treasure carriage to the vermillion steps; historiographers placed the Veritable Records on the table and then joined the ranks.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚官奏進《實錄》，序班舉《實錄》案，以次由殿中門入，班首由左門入。

translations.literal: Ceremonial officials reported the presentation of the Veritable Records; ushers lifted the Veritable Records table and entered in order through the central hall gate, the rank leader through the left gate.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial officials announced the presentation of the Veritable Records; ushers carried the Veritable Records table in through the central hall gate in order, the rank leader through the left gate.

sentences.zh: 帝興，序班以《實錄》案置於殿中。

translations.literal: The emperor rose; ushers placed the Veritable Records table in the center of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose; ushers placed the Veritable Records table in the center of the hall.

sentences.zh: 班首跪於案前，贊史官皆跪。

translations.literal: The rank leader knelt before the table; the herald called for all historiographers to kneel.
translations.idiomatic: The rank leader knelt before the table; the herald called for all historiographers to kneel.

sentences.zh: 序班並內侍官舉《實錄》案入謹身殿，置於中。

translations.literal: Ushers together with inner attendants lifted the Veritable Records table into the Hall of Self-Cultivation and placed it in the center.
translations.idiomatic: Ushers and inner attendants carried the Veritable Records table into the Hall of Self-Cultivation and placed it in the center.

sentences.zh: 帝復座。

translations.literal: The emperor resumed his seat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resumed his seat.

sentences.zh: 贊俯伏，班首俯伏，興。

translations.literal: The herald called "prostrate"; the rank leader prostrated and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The herald called "prostrate"; the rank leader prostrated and rose.

sentences.zh: 復位，贊四拜。

translations.literal: He returned to his place; the herald called for four prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to his place; the herald called for four prostrations.

sentences.zh: 贊進表，序班舉表案，由左門入，置於殿中。

translations.literal: The herald called for presentation of the memorial; ushers lifted the memorial table, entered through the left gate, and placed it in the center of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The herald called for presentation of the memorial; ushers carried the memorial table in through the left gate and placed it in the center of the hall.

sentences.zh: 贊宣表，贊衆官皆跪。

translations.literal: The herald called for proclamation of the memorial; the herald called for all officials to kneel.
translations.idiomatic: The herald called for proclamation of the memorial and for all officials to kneel.

sentences.zh: 宣訖，俯伏，興，四拜，進《實錄》官退於東班，百官入班。

translations.literal: When the proclamation was finished, they prostrated and rose, performed four prostrations; the officials who had presented the Veritable Records withdrew to the eastern rank, and all officials entered their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: After the proclamation they prostrated and rose, made four prostrations; the officials who had presented the Veritable Records withdrew to the eastern rank, and all officials took their places.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚官奏慶賀，各官四拜興。

translations.literal: Ceremonial officials reported congratulations; each official performed four prostrations and rose.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial officials announced congratulations; each official made four prostrations and rose.

sentences.zh: 贊有制，史官仍入班。

translations.literal: The herald announced that there was an imperial command; historiographers again entered the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The herald announced an imperial command; historiographers again joined the ranks.

sentences.zh: 贊跪，宣制云：「太祖高皇帝、高皇后功德光華，纂述詳實。

translations.literal: The herald called to kneel; the command was proclaimed: "The meritorious virtue of Taizu the High Emperor and the High Empress shines forth; the compilation is detailed and true."
translations.idiomatic: The herald called to kneel; the command was proclaimed: "The meritorious virtue of Taizu the High Emperor and the High Empress shines forth; the compilation is detailed and true."

sentences.zh: 朕心歡慶，與卿等同之。

translations.literal: "My heart rejoices and celebrates, and I share this with you all."
translations.idiomatic: "My heart rejoices, and I share this with you all."

sentences.zh: 」宣訖，俯伏興，三舞蹈，又四拜，禮畢。

translations.literal: " When the proclamation was finished, they prostrated and rose, performed three dances, again four prostrations, and the rites were complete.
translations.idiomatic: " After the proclamation they prostrated and rose, performed three dances, made four more prostrations, and the rites were complete.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年，《世祖實錄》成，續定進儀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli, the Veritable Records of Shizu were completed, and the presentation protocol was revised.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 5 the Veritable Records of Shizu were completed, and the presentation protocol was revised.

sentences.zh: 設寶輿、香亭、表亭於史館前，帝袞冕御中極殿，百官朝服侍班。

translations.literal: A treasure carriage, incense pavilion, and memorial pavilion were set before the Historiography Office; the emperor in full ceremonial robes attended the Central Ultimate Hall; officials in court dress stood in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: A treasure carriage, incense pavilion, and memorial pavilion were set before the Historiography Office; the emperor in full ceremonial robes took the Central Ultimate Hall; officials in court dress stood in attendance.

sentences.zh: 監修、總裁、纂修等官，朝服至館前。

translations.literal: Supervising compilers, chief compilers, and compiling officials in court dress came before the office.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising compilers, chief compilers, and compiling officials in court dress came before the office.

sentences.zh: 監修官捧表置表亭中，纂修官捧《實錄》置寶輿中，鴻臚官導迎。

translations.literal: The supervising compiler bore the memorial and placed it in the memorial pavilion; compiling officials bore the Veritable Records and placed them in the treasure carriage; Ceremonial officials led the escort.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising compiler placed the memorial in the memorial pavilion; compiling officials placed the Veritable Records in the treasure carriage; Ceremonial officials led the escort.

sentences.zh: 用鼓樂傘蓋，由會極門下階，至橋南，由中道行。

translations.literal: With drums, music, and parasols, they descended the steps of the Gate of Converging Ultimate to south of the bridge and proceeded along the central way.
translations.idiomatic: With drums, music, and parasols they descended the steps of the Gate of Converging Ultimate to south of the bridge and proceeded along the central path.

sentences.zh: 監修、總裁等官隨表亭後，由二橋行至皇極門。

translations.literal: Supervising and chief compilers followed behind the memorial pavilion, passed the two bridges, and went to the Gate of Imperial Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising and chief compilers followed the memorial pavilion across the two bridges to the Gate of Imperial Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 《實錄》輿由中門入，表亭由左門入，至丹墀案前。

translations.literal: The Veritable Records carriage entered through the central gate; the memorial pavilion through the left gate; both reached the tables before the vermillion courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records carriage entered through the central gate and the memorial pavilion through the left gate, both reaching the tables before the vermillion courtyard.

sentences.zh: 監修官捧表置於案，纂修官捧《實錄》置於案，俱侍立於石墀東。

translations.literal: The supervising compiler bore the memorial and placed it on the table; compiling officials bore the Veritable Records and placed them on the table; all stood in attendance on the east of the stone courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising compiler placed the memorial on the table and compiling officials placed the Veritable Records on the table; all stood in attendance to the east of the stone courtyard.

sentences.zh: 內殿百官行記訖，帝出御皇極殿。

translations.literal: When the inner-hall officials had finished their procession, the emperor came forth to attend the Gate of Imperial Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: When the inner-hall officials had finished their procession, the emperor came forth to the Gate of Imperial Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 監修、總裁等官入，進《實錄》、進表俱如永樂儀。

translations.literal: Supervising and chief compilers entered; presentation of the Veritable Records and the memorial were both as in the Yongle protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising and chief compilers entered; presentation of the Veritable Records and the memorial followed the Yongle protocol.

sentences.zh: 次日，司禮監官自內殿送《實錄》下殿，仍置寶輿中，用傘蓋，與監修總裁官同送皇史宬尊藏。

translations.literal: The next day, Directorate of Ceremonial officials from the inner hall escorted the Veritable Records down from the hall, again placed them in the treasure carriage, used parasols, and together with supervising and chief compilers escorted them to the Imperial History Vault for honored storage.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Directorate of Ceremonial officials escorted the Veritable Records down from the inner hall, placed them again in the treasure carriage under parasols, and together with supervising and chief compilers conveyed them to the Imperial History Vault for honored storage.

sentences.zh: ○進表箋儀

translations.literal: Protocol for presenting memorials and formal letters.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting memorials and formal letters.

sentences.zh: 明初定制，凡王府遇聖節及冬至、正旦，先期陳設畢。

translations.literal: In the regulations fixed at the beginning of Ming, whenever a princely establishment encountered the emperor's birthday, the winter solstice, or New Year's Day, arrangements were completed in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Under regulations fixed at the beginning of Ming, whenever a princely establishment observed the emperor's birthday, the winter solstice, or New Year's Day, arrangements were completed in advance.

sentences.zh: 王冕服就位四拜，詣香案前跪。

translations.literal: The prince in full ceremonial robes took his place and performed four prostrations, then went before the incense table and knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, in full court regalia, took his place and made four prostrations, then went before the incense table and knelt.

sentences.zh: 進表訖，復位，四拜，三舞蹈，山呼，又四拜。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, he returned to his place, performed four prostrations, three dances, the mountain call, and again four prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: After presenting the memorial he returned to his place, made four prostrations, three dances, the mountain call, and four more prostrations.

sentences.zh: 百官朝服隨班行禮。

translations.literal: The officials in court dress followed the ranks in performing the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in court dress followed the ranks in performing the rites.

sentences.zh: 進中宮箋儀如之，惟不舞蹈山呼。

translations.literal: The protocol for presenting a formal letter to the central palace was the same, except that there was no dancing or mountain call.
translations.idiomatic: The protocol for presenting a formal letter to the empress was the same, except without dancing or the mountain call.

sentences.zh: 進皇太子箋，王皮弁服，行八拜禮，百官朝服隨班行禮。

translations.literal: For presenting a formal letter to the crown prince, the prince wore the leather cap and performed the eight-prostration rite; officials in court dress followed the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: For presenting a formal letter to the crown prince, the prince wore the leather cap and performed eight prostrations; officials in court dress followed the ranks.

sentences.zh: 凡進賀表箋，皇子封王者，於天子前自稱曰：「第幾子某王某」，稱天子曰：「父皇陛下」，皇后曰：「母后殿下」。

translations.literal: For all congratulatory memorials and formal letters, when an imperial son was enfeoffed as prince, before the Son of Heaven he styled himself: "the such-and-such son, Prince So-and-so," styled the Son of Heaven: "Imperial Father, Your Majesty," and the empress: "Imperial Mother, Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: For all congratulatory memorials and formal letters, when an imperial son was enfeoffed as prince, before the emperor he styled himself "the such-and-such son, Prince So-and-so," the emperor as "Imperial Father, Your Majesty," and the empress as "Imperial Mother, Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 若孫，則自稱曰：「第幾孫某王某」，稱天子曰：「祖父皇帝陛下，。

translations.literal: If a grandson, he styled himself: "the such-and-such grandson, Prince So-and-so," and styled the Son of Heaven: "Grandfather Emperor, Your Majesty,"
translations.idiomatic: If a grandson, he styled himself "the such-and-such grandson, Prince So-and-so," and the emperor as "Grandfather Emperor, Your Majesty,"

sentences.zh: 」皇后曰：「祖母皇后殿下」。

translations.literal: " and the empress: "Grandmother Empress, Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: " and the empress as "Grandmother Empress, Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 若弟，則自稱曰：「第幾弟某封某」，稱天子曰：「大兄皇帝陛下」，皇后曰：「尊嫂皇后殿下」。

translations.literal: If a younger brother, he styled himself: "the such-and-such younger brother, enfeoffed as such-and-such," styled the Son of Heaven: "Elder Brother Emperor, Your Majesty," and the empress: "Honored Sister-in-law Empress, Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: If a younger brother, he styled himself "the such-and-such younger brother, enfeoffed as such-and-such," the emperor as "Elder Brother Emperor, Your Majesty," and the empress as "Honored Sister-in-law Empress, Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 侄則自稱曰：「第幾侄某封某」，稱天子曰：「伯父皇帝陛下」，「叔父皇帝陛下」，皇后曰：「伯母皇后殿下」，「叔母皇后殿下」。

translations.literal: If a nephew, he styled himself: "the such-and-such nephew, enfeoffed as such-and-such," styled the Son of Heaven: "Paternal-uncle Emperor, Your Majesty," or "Maternal-uncle Emperor, Your Majesty," and the empress: "Paternal-aunt Empress, Your Highness," or "Maternal-aunt Empress, Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: If a nephew, he styled himself "the such-and-such nephew, enfeoffed as such-and-such," the emperor as "Paternal-uncle Emperor, Your Majesty" or "Maternal-uncle Emperor, Your Majesty," and the empress as "Paternal-aunt Empress, Your Highness" or "Maternal-aunt Empress, Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 若尊屬，則自稱曰：「某封臣某」，稱天子曰：「皇帝陛下」，皇后曰：「皇后殿下」。

translations.literal: If a senior kinsman, he styled himself: "such-and-such enfeoffment, subject So-and-so," styled the Son of Heaven: "Emperor, Your Majesty," and the empress: "Empress, Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: If a senior kinsman, he styled himself "such-and-such enfeoffment, subject So-and-so," the emperor as "Emperor, Your Majesty," and the empress as "Empress, Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 若從孫以下，則稱「從孫、再從孫、三從孫某封某」，皆稱皇帝皇后曰：「伯祖、叔祖皇帝陛下」，「伯祖母、叔祖母皇后殿下」。

translations.literal: If a collateral grandson or below, he styled himself "collateral grandson," "second collateral grandson," or "third collateral grandson, enfeoffed as such-and-such," and all styled the emperor and empress: "Paternal-great-uncle or maternal-great-uncle Emperor, Your Majesty," and "Paternal-great-aunt or maternal-great-aunt Empress, Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: If a collateral grandson or below, he styled himself "collateral grandson," "second collateral grandson," or "third collateral grandson, enfeoffed as such-and-such," and all styled the emperor and empress as "Paternal-great-uncle or maternal-great-uncle Emperor, Your Majesty" and "Paternal-great-aunt or maternal-great-aunt Empress, Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 至世宗時，始令各王府表箋，俱用聖號，不得用家人禮。

translations.literal: By the time of Shizong, it was first ordered that memorials and formal letters from all princely establishments use the sacred titles and must not use family-style forms of address.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of the Shizong Emperor, all princely memorials and formal letters were ordered to use the sacred titles and not family-style forms of address.

sentences.zh: 凡在外百官進賀表箋，前一日，結綵於公廨及街衢。

translations.literal: For all officials outside the capital presenting congratulatory memorials and formal letters, on the previous day colored hangings were tied at the government compound and along the streets.
translations.idiomatic: For all officials outside the capital presenting congratulatory memorials and formal letters, colored hangings were put up the day before at the government compound and along the streets.

sentences.zh: 文武官各齋沐，宿本署。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials each purified themselves and lodged at their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials each purified themselves and lodged at their offices.

sentences.zh: 清晨，設龍亭於庭中，設儀仗鼓樂於露臺，設表箋案於龍亭前，香案於表箋案前，設進表箋官位於龍亭東。

translations.literal: At dawn, a dragon pavilion was set in the courtyard; guard of honor and drums and music on the open terrace; memorial and formal-letter tables before the dragon pavilion; an incense table before the memorial tables; the position for the memorial-presenting officer to the east of the dragon pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn a dragon pavilion was set in the courtyard, guard of honor and music on the open terrace, memorial tables before the dragon pavilion, an incense table before them, and the memorial-presenting officer's station to the east of the dragon pavilion.

sentences.zh: 鼓初嚴，各官具服。

translations.literal: At the first drum signal of vigil, each official donned full dress.
translations.idiomatic: At the first drum signal each official donned full dress.

sentences.zh: 次嚴，班首具服詣香案前，滌印用印訖，以表箋置於案，退立幕次。

translations.literal: At the second signal, the rank leader in full dress went before the incense table, washed the seal and applied it, placed the memorial and formal letter on the table, and withdrew to stand in the side pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At the second signal the rank leader in full dress went before the incense table, washed and applied the seal, placed the memorial and formal letter on the table, and withdrew to the side pavilion.

sentences.zh: 三嚴，各官入班四拜，班首詣香案前。

translations.literal: At the third signal, each official entered the ranks and performed four prostrations; the rank leader went before the incense table.
translations.idiomatic: At the third signal each official entered the ranks and made four prostrations; the rank leader went before the incense table.

sentences.zh: 贊跪，衆官皆跪。

translations.literal: The herald called to kneel; all officials knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The herald called to kneel; all officials knelt.

sentences.zh: 執事者以表箋跪授班首，班首跪授進表官，進表官跪受，置龍亭中。

translations.literal: Attendants knelt and handed the memorial and formal letter to the rank leader; the rank leader knelt and handed them to the memorial-presenting officer; the presenting officer knelt to receive them and placed them in the dragon pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants knelt and handed the memorial and formal letter to the rank leader, who knelt and handed them to the presenting officer, who knelt to receive them and placed them in the dragon pavilion.

sentences.zh: 班首復位，各官皆四拜，三舞蹈，山呼，四拜。

translations.literal: The rank leader returned to his place; all officials performed four prostrations, three dances, the mountain call, and four prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: The rank leader returned to his place; all officials made four prostrations, three dances, the mountain call, and four prostrations.

sentences.zh: 金鼓儀仗鼓樂百官前導，進表官在龍亭後東。

translations.literal: Gongs, drums, guard of honor, drums and music, and officials led in advance; the memorial-presenting officer was to the east behind the dragon pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Gongs, drums, guard of honor, music, and officials led the way; the presenting officer stood to the east behind the dragon pavilion.

sentences.zh: 至郊外，置龍亭南向，儀仗鼓樂陳列如前，文武官侍立。

translations.literal: At the suburban outskirts, the dragon pavilion was set facing south; guard of honor and drums and music were arrayed as before; civil and military officials stood in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban outskirts the dragon pavilion was set facing south, guard of honor and music arrayed as before, and civil and military officials stood in attendance.

sentences.zh: 班首取表箋授進表官，進表官就於馬上受表，即行，百官退。

translations.literal: The rank leader took the memorial and formal letter and handed them to the presenting officer; the presenting officer received the memorial mounted and at once set out; the officials withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rank leader handed the memorial and formal letter to the presenting officer, who received the memorial mounted and set out at once; the officials withdrew.

sentences.zh: ○鄉飲酒禮

translations.literal: Village drinking ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The village drinking rite.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「鄉飲酒之禮廢，則爭鬥之獄繁矣。

translations.literal: The Record says: "When the village drinking ceremony is abandoned, lawsuits of strife and contention multiply."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "When the village drinking rite is abandoned, lawsuits of strife and contention multiply."

sentences.zh: 」故《儀禮》所記，惟鄉飲之禮達於庶民。

translations.literal: " Therefore among what the Ceremonial Rites records, only the village drinking rite reaches down to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore among what the Ceremonial Rites records, only the village drinking rite reaches down to the common people.

sentences.zh: 自周迄明，損益代殊，而其禮不廢。

translations.literal: From Zhou down to Ming, additions and subtractions differed by age, yet the rite was not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhou down to Ming the rite was revised age by age, yet it was never abandoned.

sentences.zh: 洪武五年，詔禮部奏定鄉飲禮儀，命有司與學官率士大夫之老者，行於學校，民間里社亦行之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongwu, an edict ordered the Ministry of Rites to report and fix the village drinking ritual; local officials and school officers were commanded to lead the elder gentry-scholars in performing it at schools, and village community altars in the populace also performed it.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 5 an edict ordered the Ministry of Rites to establish the village drinking ritual; local officials and school officers were to lead elder gentry-scholars in performing it at schools, and village community altars among the populace did so as well.

sentences.zh: 十六年，詔班《鄉飲酒禮圖式》於天下，每歲正月十五日、十月初一日，於儒學行之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, an edict promulgated the Diagram of the Village Drinking Ceremony throughout the realm; on the fifteenth day of the first month and the first day of the tenth month each year, it was performed at Confucian schools.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 an edict distributed the Diagram of the Village Drinking Ceremony empire-wide; each year on the fifteenth day of the first month and the first day of the tenth month it was performed at county schools.

sentences.zh: 其儀，以府州縣長吏爲主，以鄉之致仕官有德行者一人爲賓。

translations.literal: The protocol: the chief magistrate of the prefecture, department, or county served as host, and one retired official of the district distinguished for virtue and conduct served as guest of honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ceremony the prefectural, departmental, or county chief magistrate served as host, and one retired district official noted for virtue and conduct served as guest of honor.

sentences.zh: 擇年高有德者爲僎賓，其次爲介，又其次爲三賓，又其次爲衆賓，教職爲司正。

translations.literal: The eldest and most virtuous was chosen as assistant guest; next ranked the intercessor, then the third guests, then the assembly of guests; the teaching staff served as marshal of the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest and most virtuous man was chosen as assistant guest, then the intercessor, then the third guests, then the general guests; school officers served as marshal of the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 贊禮、贊引、讀律，皆使能者。

translations.literal: Ritual announcer, usher, and reader of statutes were all assigned to capable men.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual announcer, usher, and statute reader were all drawn from men of ability.

sentences.zh: 前期，設賓席於堂北兩楹之間，少西，南面；

translations.literal: In advance, the guest's mat was set between the northern pillars of the hall, slightly west, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand the guest's seat was placed between the hall's northern pillars, slightly west, facing south;

sentences.zh: 主席於阼階上，西面；

translations.literal: the host's mat on the eastern steps, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: the host's seat on the eastern steps, facing west;

sentences.zh: 介席於西階上，東面；

translations.literal: the intercessor's mat on the western steps, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: the intercessor's seat on the western steps, facing east;

sentences.zh: 僎席於賓東，南面；

translations.literal: the assistant guest's mat east of the guest, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: the assistant guest's seat east of the guest, facing south;

sentences.zh: 三賓席於賓西，南面。

translations.literal: the third guests' mats west of the guest, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: the third guests' seats west of the guest, facing south.

sentences.zh: 皆專席不屬。

translations.literal: Each had a separate mat, not shared.
translations.idiomatic: Each had an individual seat, not adjoining another's.

sentences.zh: 衆賓六十以上者，席於西序，東面北上。

translations.literal: Assembly guests sixty years of age and above were seated in the western wing, facing east, arrayed northward.
translations.idiomatic: General guests aged sixty and above sat in the western wing, facing east and ranked from south to north.

sentences.zh: 賓多則設席於西階，北面東上；

translations.literal: If guests were numerous, mats were also set on the western steps, facing north, arrayed eastward;
translations.idiomatic: If there were many guests, seats were also set on the western steps, facing north and ranked from west to east;

sentences.zh: 僚佐席於東序，西面北上。

translations.literal: staff assistants were seated in the eastern wing, facing west, arrayed northward.
translations.idiomatic: staff assistants sat in the eastern wing, facing west and ranked from south to north.

sentences.zh: 設衆賓五十以下者位於堂下西階之西，當序，東面北上。

translations.literal: Positions for assembly guests under fifty were set west of the western steps below the hall, aligned with the wing, facing east, arrayed northward.
translations.idiomatic: Places for general guests under fifty were set below the hall west of the western steps, level with the wing, facing east and ranked from south to north.

sentences.zh: 賓多則又設位於西階之南，北面東上。

translations.literal: If guests were numerous, positions were also set south of the western steps, facing north, arrayed eastward.
translations.idiomatic: If there were many guests, places were also set south of the western steps, facing north and ranked from west to east.

sentences.zh: 司正及讀律者，位於堂下阼階之南，北面西上。

translations.literal: The marshal and the reader of statutes were positioned south of the eastern steps below the hall, facing north, arrayed westward.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal and statute reader stood below the hall south of the eastern steps, facing north and ranked from east to west.

sentences.zh: 設主之贊者位於阼階之東，西面北上。

translations.literal: The host's assistants were positioned east of the eastern steps, facing west, arrayed northward.
translations.idiomatic: The host's ushers stood east of the eastern steps, facing west and ranked from south to north.

sentences.zh: 設主及僚佐以下次於東廊，賓介及衆賓次於庠門之外，僎次亦在門外。

translations.literal: The host and staff assistants were ordered in the eastern corridor; the guest, intercessor, and assembly of guests were ordered outside the school gate; the assistant guest's station was also outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The host and staff waited in the eastern corridor; the guest, intercessor, and general guests waited outside the school gate; the assistant guest also waited outside.

sentences.zh: 設酒尊於堂上東南隅，加勺冪，用葛巾；

translations.literal: A wine vessel was set in the southeastern corner of the hall, fitted with ladle and cover, using a hemp cloth;
translations.idiomatic: A wine jar was placed in the hall's southeastern corner, with ladle and cover draped in hemp cloth;

sentences.zh: 爵洗於阼階下東南；

translations.literal: the goblet-washing basin southeast of the bottom of the eastern steps;
translations.idiomatic: the goblet-washing basin southeast below the eastern steps;

sentences.zh: 篚一於洗西，實以爵觶；

translations.literal: one basket west of the basin, filled with goblets and cups;
translations.idiomatic: one basket west of the basin, holding goblets and cups;

sentences.zh: 盥洗在爵洗東。

translations.literal: the hand-washing basin east of the goblet-washing basin.
translations.idiomatic: the hand-washing basin stood east of the goblet-washing basin.

sentences.zh: 設卓案於堂上下席位前，陳豆於其上。

translations.literal: High tables were set before each seat above and below the hall, with dishes placed upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Tables were set before each seat above and below the hall, with dishes laid out upon them.

sentences.zh: 六十者三豆，七十者四豆，八十者五豆，九十者六豆，堂下者二豆。

translations.literal: Sixty-year-olds received three dishes, seventy-year-olds four, eighty-year-olds five, ninety-year-olds six; those below the hall received two.
translations.idiomatic: A man of sixty received three dishes, of seventy four, of eighty five, of ninety six; those below the hall received two.

sentences.zh: 主人豆如賓之數，皆實以菹醢。

translations.literal: The host's dishes matched the guest's number; all were filled with pickled meats and relishes.
translations.idiomatic: The host's dishes matched the guest's count; all were filled with pickled meats and relishes.

sentences.zh: 至期，賓將及門，執事者進報曰：「賓至。

translations.literal: When the day arrived and the guest was about to reach the gate, the attendants came forward and reported: "The guest has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came and the guest was nearing the gate, attendants stepped forward and announced: "The guest has arrived.

sentences.zh: 」主人率僚屬出迎於門外，主西面，賓以下皆東面。

translations.literal: " The host led his staff out to welcome them outside the gate; the host faced west, and the guest and those below all faced east.
translations.idiomatic: " The host led his staff out to welcome them beyond the gate; the host faced west, the guest and all below him faced east.

sentences.zh: 三揖三讓，而後升堂，相向再拜，升坐。

translations.literal: Three bows and three deferrals, then they ascended the hall, bowed facing each other twice, and took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: After three bows and three deferrals they ascended the hall, exchanged two facing bows, and sat down.

sentences.zh: 執事者報僎至，迎坐如前儀。
