translations.literal: Attendants reported the assistant guest's arrival; he was welcomed and seated according to the same protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants announced the assistant guest's arrival; he was welcomed and seated by the same protocol.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱司正揚觶。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer called for the marshal to raise the cup.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer called for the marshal to raise the goblet.

sentences.zh: 司正詣盥洗位，次詣爵洗位，取觶於篚，洗觶。

translations.literal: The marshal went to the hand-washing station, then to the goblet-washing station, took a cup from the basket, and washed it.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal went to the hand-washing place, then to the goblet-washing place, took a cup from the basket, and washed it.

sentences.zh: 升自西階，詣尊所酌酒，進兩楹之間，北面立。

translations.literal: He ascended by the western steps, went to the wine vessel to pour, advanced to between the two pillars, and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended the western steps, poured wine at the jar, advanced between the two pillars, and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 在坐者皆起，司正揖，僎賓以下皆報揖。

translations.literal: All seated rose; the marshal bowed, and the assistant guest and those below all returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: All who were seated rose; the marshal bowed, and the assistant guest and all below returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 司正乃舉觶，言曰：「恭惟朝廷，率由舊章。

translations.literal: The marshal then raised the cup and spoke: "Reverently consider that the court follows the ancient statutes.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal then raised the goblet and said: "Reverently consider that the court follows the ancient statutes.

sentences.zh: 敦崇禮教，舉行鄉飲，非爲飲食。

translations.literal: We promote and uphold ritual teaching and conduct the village drinking rite; it is not for the sake of eating and drinking.
translations.idiomatic: We promote ritual teaching and hold the village drinking ceremony; it is not for food and drink alone.

sentences.zh: 凡我長幼，各相勸勉。

translations.literal: All of us, elder and younger, should each exhort and encourage one another.
translations.idiomatic: All of us, elder and younger, should exhort and encourage one another.

sentences.zh: 爲臣竭忠，爲子盡孝，長幼有序，兄友弟恭。

translations.literal: As subjects, render full loyalty; as sons, render full filial piety; let elder and younger keep their order; let elder brothers be friendly and younger brothers respectful.
translations.idiomatic: As subjects give full loyalty; as sons give full filial piety; let elder and younger keep their order; let elder brothers be friendly and younger brothers deferential.

sentences.zh: 內睦宗族，外和鄉里，無或廢墜，以忝所生。

translations.literal: Be harmonious within the clan and concordant with neighbors abroad; let none fall into neglect and disgrace those who bore them.
translations.idiomatic: Be harmonious within the clan and at peace with neighbors abroad; let none neglect these duties and disgrace those who gave them life.

sentences.zh: 」言畢，贊禮唱司正飲酒。

translations.literal: " When the words were finished, the ritual announcer called for the marshal to drink.
translations.idiomatic: " When he had finished speaking, the ritual announcer called for the marshal to drink.

sentences.zh: 飲畢，揖報如初。

translations.literal: When he had finished drinking, bows were exchanged as at first.
translations.idiomatic: When the drinking was finished, bows were exchanged as before.

sentences.zh: 司正復位，僎賓以下皆坐。

translations.literal: The marshal returned to his place; the assistant guest and those below all sat down.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal returned to his station; the assistant guest and all below sat down.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱讀律令，執事舉律令案於堂之中。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer called for the reading of statutes; attendants raised the statute case to the center of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer called for the reading of statutes; attendants carried the statute case to the center of the hall.

sentences.zh: 讀律令者詣案前，北向立讀，皆如揚觶儀。

translations.literal: The reader of statutes went before the case, stood facing north, and read; all was as in the protocol for raising the cup.
translations.idiomatic: The statute reader went before the case, stood facing north, and read; the ceremony matched that for raising the goblet.

sentences.zh: 有過之人俱赴正席立聽，讀畢復位。

translations.literal: Those who had committed offenses all came to the main seats to stand and listen; when the reading was finished they returned to their places.
translations.idiomatic: All who had committed offenses came forward to the main seats to stand and listen; when the reading was done they returned to their places.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱供饌，執事者舉饌案至賓前，次僎，次介，次主，三賓以下各以次舉訖。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer called for the serving of food; attendants carried food trays to the guest, then the assistant guest, then the intercessor, then the host; from the third guests downward each was served in order until complete.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer called for food to be served; attendants brought trays first to the guest, then the assistant guest, intercessor, and host; from the third guests downward each was served in turn until all were done.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱獻賓，主降詣盥洗及爵洗位，洗爵酌酒，至賓前，置於席。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer called for the host's presentation to the guest; the host descended, went to the hand-washing and goblet-washing stations, washed the goblet and poured wine, came before the guest, and placed it on the mat.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer called for the host to present wine to the guest; the host descended, washed at the hand-washing and goblet-washing places, poured wine, came before the guest, and set the goblet on his seat.

sentences.zh: 稍退，兩拜，賓答拜。

translations.literal: He withdrew slightly, bowed twice; the guest returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew a step, bowed twice, and the guest returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 又詣僎前，亦如之。

translations.literal: He then went before the assistant guest and did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: He then did the same before the assistant guest.

sentences.zh: 主退復位。

translations.literal: The host withdrew and returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: The host withdrew and returned to his seat.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱賓酬酒，賓起，僎從之，詣盥洗爵洗位如儀。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer called for the guest's return toast; the guest rose, the assistant guest followed, and they went to the hand-washing and goblet-washing stations as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer called for the guest to return the toast; the guest rose, the assistant guest followed, and both went to the hand-washing and goblet-washing places as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 至主前，置爵。

translations.literal: They came before the host and placed the goblet.
translations.idiomatic: They came before the host and set down the goblet.

sentences.zh: 賓、僎、主皆再拜，各就坐。

translations.literal: Guest, assistant guest, and host all bowed twice and each took his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Guest, assistant guest, and host all bowed twice and resumed their seats.

sentences.zh: 執事者於介、三賓、衆賓以下，以次斟酒訖。

translations.literal: Attendants poured wine for the intercessor, third guests, assembly of guests, and those below, each in order until finished.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants poured wine for the intercessor, third guests, general guests, and those below, each in turn until all were served.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱飲酒，或三行，或五行。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer called for drinking; three rounds or five rounds were made.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer called for drinking; three rounds or five rounds were observed.

sentences.zh: 供湯三品畢。

translations.literal: Three kinds of broth were served, and that was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Three rounds of hot water were served, and that concluded the course.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱徹饌，在坐者皆興。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer called for the removal of the food; all seated rose.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer called for the food to be cleared; all who were seated rose.

sentences.zh: 僎、主、僚屬居東，賓、介、三賓、衆賓居西，皆再拜。

translations.literal: The assistant guest, host, and staff stood to the east; the guest, intercessor, third guests, and assembly of guests stood to the west; all bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant guest, host, and staff stood on the east; the guest, intercessor, third guests, and general guests on the west; all bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱送賓，以次下堂，分東西行，仍三揖出庠門而退。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer called for escorting the guest; they descended the hall in order, divided east and west, and with three more bows exited the school gate and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer called for the guest to be escorted out; they descended in order, divided east and west, bowed three times again, and withdrew through the school gate.

sentences.zh: 里中鄉飲略同。

translations.literal: Village drinking in the community was substantially the same.
translations.idiomatic: Village drinking in the neighborhoods followed much the same form.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，命凡有過犯之人列於外坐，同類者成席，不許雜於善良之中，著爲令。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, it was ordered that all who had committed offenses were to be ranked in outer seats; those of the same category formed a group, and they were not permitted to mix among the virtuous; this was established as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 it was ordered that anyone who had committed an offense was seated in the outer ranks; those of the same kind formed a separate group and were not allowed to sit among the virtuous; this was written into law.

sentences.zh: 三曰賓禮，以待蕃國之君長與其使者。

translations.literal: Third are guest rites, to receive the sovereigns of foreign states and their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Third are guest rites, for receiving the rulers of foreign states and their envoys.

sentences.zh: 宋政和間，詳定五禮，取《周官·司儀》掌九儀賓客擯相，詔王南鄉以朝諸侯之義，故以朝會儀列爲賓禮。

translations.literal: During the Zhenghe reign of Song, the Five Rites were fixed in detail; taking from the Offices of Zhou · Protocol Master the authority over the nine ceremonies for receiving and ushering guests, and the principle of the king facing south to receive the feudal lords, court audience ceremony was therefore arranged as guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe reign of Song the Five Rites were fixed in detail; drawing on the Offices of Zhou · Protocol Master, which governs the nine ceremonies for receiving and ushering guests, and on the principle of the king facing south to receive the feudal lords, court audience ceremony was therefore classified as guest rites.

sentences.zh: 按古之諸侯，各君其國，子其民，待以客禮可也，不可與後世之臣下等。

translations.literal: Considering antiquity, each feudal lord ruled his own state and regarded his people as children; to treat them with guest ceremony was proper; they could not be equated with later subjects.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity each feudal lord ruled his own state and cherished his people as children; guest ceremony was appropriate for them and they could not be treated like later subjects.

sentences.zh: 茲改從其舊，而百官庶人相見之禮附焉。

translations.literal: Here the old arrangement is restored, and the ceremonies for meetings among officials and commoners are appended.
translations.idiomatic: Here the former arrangement is restored, with ceremonies for meetings among officials and commoners appended.

sentences.zh: ○蕃王朝貢禮

translations.literal: Tributary audience of foreign kings.
translations.idiomatic: Tributary audience of foreign kings.

sentences.zh: 蕃王入朝，其迎勞宴饗之禮，惟唐製爲詳。

translations.literal: When a foreign king came to court, the protocol for welcoming, comforting, banqueting, and entertaining was most detailed in the Tang regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When a foreign king came to court, the protocols for welcoming, comforting, banqueting, and entertaining were most fully set out under the Tang.

sentences.zh: 宋時，蕃國皆遣使入貢，所接見惟使臣而已。

translations.literal: In Song times foreign states all sent envoys to present tribute; those received in audience were only the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In Song times foreign states sent envoys to present tribute; only the envoys were received in audience.

sentences.zh: 明洪武二年定制：凡蕃王至龍江驛，遣侍儀、通贊二人接伴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongwu of Ming regulations were fixed: whenever a foreign king reached Longjiang Station, two ceremony masters and protocol announcers were dispatched to receive and accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2 regulations were fixed: whenever a foreign king reached Longjiang Station, two masters of ceremony and protocol announcers were sent to receive and accompany him.

sentences.zh: 館人陳蕃王座於廳西北，東向。

translations.literal: The station keeper set out the foreign king's seat in the northwest of the hall, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The station keeper placed the foreign king's seat in the northwest of the hall, facing east.

sentences.zh: 應天府知府出迎，設座於廳東南，西向。

translations.literal: The prefect of Yingtian Prefecture came out to welcome him and set a seat in the southeast of the hall, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Yingtian came out to welcome him and set a seat in the southeast of the hall, facing west.

sentences.zh: 以賓主接見。

translations.literal: They met as host and guest.
translations.idiomatic: They met as host and guest.

sentences.zh: 宴畢，知府還，蕃王送於門外。

translations.literal: When the banquet was finished, the prefect departed, and the foreign king saw him off outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet was over the prefect withdrew, and the foreign king saw him off at the gate.

sentences.zh: 明日，接伴官送蕃王入會同館，禮部尚書即館宴勞。

translations.literal: The next day the receiving officers escorted the foreign king into the Reception Hall; the Minister of Rites banqueted and comforted him at the hall itself.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the receiving officers escorted the foreign king to the Reception Hall, where the Minister of Rites banqueted and comforted him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 尚書至，蕃王服其國服相見。

translations.literal: When the minister arrived, the foreign king wore his national dress to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When the minister arrived, the foreign king wore his national dress to receive him.

sentences.zh: 宴饗迎送俱如龍江驛。

translations.literal: Banquet, entertainment, welcoming, and send-off were all as at Longjiang Station.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet, entertainment, welcoming, and send-off all followed the Longjiang Station protocol.

sentences.zh: 酒行，用樂。

translations.literal: When wine was served, music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When wine was served, music was played.

sentences.zh: 明日，中書省奏聞，命官一員詣館，如前宴勞。

translations.literal: The next day the Secretariat reported to the throne, and an official was appointed to go to the hall and banquet and comfort him as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Secretariat reported to the throne, and an official was appointed to go to the hall and banquet him as before.

sentences.zh: 侍儀司以蕃王及從官具服，於天界寺習儀三日，擇日朝見。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Ceremonies had the foreign king and his attendant officials fully robed; they practiced the ceremony at Tianjie Temple for three days, then a day was chosen for the court audience.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Ceremonies had the foreign king and his attendants fully robed; they rehearsed the ceremony at Tianjie Temple for three days, then a day was chosen for the court audience.

sentences.zh: 設蕃王及從官次於午門外，蕃王拜位於丹墀中道，稍西，從官在其後。

translations.literal: Stations for the foreign king and attendant officials were set outside the Meridian Gate; the foreign king's bowing position was on the central path of the Red Steps, slightly west, with attendant officials behind him.
translations.idiomatic: Stations for the foreign king and his attendants were set outside the Meridian Gate; the foreign king's bowing place was on the central path of the Red Steps, slightly west, with his attendants behind him.

sentences.zh: 設方物案于丹墀中道東西。

translations.literal: Tables for tribute goods were set east and west on the central path of the Red Steps.
translations.idiomatic: Tables for tribute goods were set east and west along the central path of the Red Steps.

sentences.zh: 知班二，位於蕃王拜位北，引蕃王舍人二，位於蕃王北，引蕃王從官舍人二，位於蕃王從官北，俱東西相向。

translations.literal: Two order-keepers were positioned north of the foreign king's bowing place; two ushers for the foreign king were positioned north of the king, and two ushers for the attendant officials north of them; all faced each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Two order-keepers stood north of the foreign king's bowing place; two ushers for the foreign king stood north of him, and two ushers for his attendants north of them; all faced one another east and west.

sentences.zh: 鼓三嚴，百官入侍。

translations.literal: At the third drum of the triple salute, the officials entered to attend.
translations.idiomatic: At the third drum of the triple salute the officials entered to attend.

sentences.zh: 執事舉方物案，蕃王隨案由西門入，至殿前丹墀西，俟立。

translations.literal: Attendants raised the tribute tables; the foreign king followed the tables in through the western gate, reaching the west of the Red Steps before the hall, and stood waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants carried in the tribute tables; the foreign king followed them through the western gate to the west side of the Red Steps before the hall and stood waiting.

sentences.zh: 皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍御殿。

translations.literal: The emperor wore the communication-crown and crimson gauze robe and took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore the communication crown and crimson gauze robe and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 蕃王及從官各就拜位，以主物案置拜位前。

translations.literal: The foreign king and attendant officials each took their bowing positions; the main tribute table was placed before the bowing position.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign king and his attendants each took their bowing places; the main tribute table was set before the bowing place.

sentences.zh: 贊四拜訖，引班導蕃王升殿。

translations.literal: When the announcement of four bows was finished, the ushering corps guided the foreign king up the hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the four bows were announced and completed, the ushering corps guided the foreign king up the hall.

sentences.zh: 宣方物官以方物狀由西陛升，入殿西門，內贊引至御前。

translations.literal: The tribute-presenting officer, carrying the inventory of tribute goods, ascended by the western steps, entered the western gate of the hall, and was led by the inner announcer to before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The tribute-presenting officer, bearing the inventory of tribute goods, ascended the western steps, entered the hall's western gate, and was led by the inner announcer before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，蕃王再拜，跪，稱賀致詞。

translations.literal: An announcer called for bowing; the foreign king bowed twice, knelt, and offered congratulations and an address.
translations.idiomatic: An announcer called for bowing; the foreign king bowed twice, knelt, and offered congratulations and a formal address.

sentences.zh: 宣方物官宣狀。

translations.literal: The tribute-presenting officer announced the inventory.
translations.idiomatic: The tribute-presenting officer read the inventory aloud.

sentences.zh: 承製官宣制訖，蕃王俯伏，興，再拜，出殿西門，復位。

translations.literal: When the edict-reciting officer had finished proclaiming the edict, the foreign king prostrated himself, rose, bowed twice, exited the western gate of the hall, and returned to his position.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict-reciting officer had finished proclaiming the edict, the foreign king prostrated himself, rose, bowed twice, left by the hall's western gate, and returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，蕃王及其從官皆四拜。

translations.literal: An announcer called for bowing; the foreign king and his attendant officials all performed four bows.
translations.idiomatic: An announcer called for bowing; the foreign king and his attendants all performed four bows.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，皇帝興，蕃王以下出。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the emperor rose, and the foreign king and those below departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete the emperor rose, and the foreign king and those below withdrew.

sentences.zh: 樂作樂止皆如常。

translations.literal: Music starting and stopping followed the usual practice.
translations.idiomatic: The starting and stopping of music followed the usual practice.

sentences.zh: 見皇太子於東宮正殿，設拜位於殿外。

translations.literal: He was received by the crown prince in the main hall of the Eastern Palace; a bowing position was set outside the hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was received by the crown prince in the Eastern Palace's main hall; a bowing place was set outside the hall.

sentences.zh: 皇太子皮弁服升座，蕃王再拜，皇太子立受。

translations.literal: The crown prince, wearing the leather cap, ascended and took the seat; the foreign king bowed twice, and the crown prince received it standing.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, wearing the leather cap, ascended and took his seat; the foreign king bowed twice, and the crown prince received the bow standing.

sentences.zh: 蕃王跪稱賀，致詞訖，復位再拜，皇太子答拜。

translations.literal: The foreign king knelt and offered congratulations; when the address was finished he returned to his position, bowed twice, and the crown prince returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign king knelt and offered congratulations; when his address was finished he returned to his place, bowed twice, and the crown prince returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 蕃王出，其從官行四拜禮。

translations.literal: When the foreign king departed, his attendant officials performed the four-bow ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When the foreign king withdrew, his attendants performed the four-bow ceremony.

sentences.zh: 見親王，東西相向再拜，王答拜。

translations.literal: In meeting imperial princes, they faced each other east and west and bowed twice; the prince returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: In meeting imperial princes they faced one another east and west, bowed twice, and the prince returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 俱就座，王座稍北。

translations.literal: Each took a seat; the prince's seat was slightly to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Each took a seat; the prince's seat was set slightly to the north.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，揖而出。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, they bowed and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete they bowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 見丞相、三公、大都督、御史大夫皆鈞禮。

translations.literal: In meeting the chancellor, the Three Dukes, the regional commander-in-chief, and the chief censor, all followed the standard mutual rite.
translations.idiomatic: In meeting the chancellor, the Three Dukes, the regional commander-in-chief, and the chief censor, all followed the standard mutual rite.

sentences.zh: 蕃王陛辭，如朝見儀，不傳制。

translations.literal: For the foreign king's farewell audience, the protocol was as for a court audience, but no edict was relayed.
translations.idiomatic: For the foreign king's farewell audience, the protocol matched a court audience, but no edict was relayed.

sentences.zh: 中書省率禮部官送龍江驛，宴如初。

translations.literal: The Secretariat led Ministry of Rites officials to escort him to Longjiang Station; the banquet was as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat led Ministry of Rites officers to escort him to Longjiang Station, with a banquet as before.

sentences.zh: 二十七年四月，以舊儀煩，命更定。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, fourth month, because the old protocol was burdensome, an order was issued to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 27, fourth month, because the old protocol had grown burdensome, an order was issued to revise it.

sentences.zh: 凡蕃國來朝，先遣禮部官勞於會同館。

translations.literal: Whenever foreign states came to court, Ministry of Rites officials were first dispatched to welcome them at the Hall of Joint Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever foreign states came to court, Ministry of Rites officers were first sent to welcome them at the Hall of Joint Harmony.

sentences.zh: 明日，各具其國服，如嘗賜朝服者則服朝服，於奉天殿朝見。

translations.literal: The next day each wore his state's dress; if court dress had previously been bestowed, they wore court dress, and had their audience at the Hall of Accepting Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The next day each wore his state's dress; those who had previously been granted court dress wore court dress, and had their audience at the Hall of Accepting Heaven.

sentences.zh: 行八拜禮畢，即詣文華殿朝皇太子，行四拜禮。

translations.literal: When the eight-bow rite was complete, they went at once to the Literary Splendor Hall to attend the crown prince, performing the four-bow rite.
translations.idiomatic: When the eight bows were complete, they went at once to the Literary Splendor Hall to attend the crown prince, performing four bows.

sentences.zh: 見親王亦如之，王立受，答後二拜。

translations.literal: In meeting imperial princes it was likewise; the prince stood to receive, and after returning the bow they bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: In meeting imperial princes it was the same: the prince stood to receive, and after the return bow they bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 從官隨蕃王后行禮。

translations.literal: Attendant officials followed the foreign king in performing the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant officials followed the foreign king in performing the rite.

sentences.zh: 凡遇宴會，蕃王居侯伯之下。

translations.literal: At banquets, the foreign king was seated below marquises and earls.
translations.idiomatic: At banquets the foreign king was seated below marquises and earls.

sentences.zh: 凡蕃國遣使朝貢，至驛，遣應天府同知禮待。

translations.literal: Whenever foreign states dispatched envoys on tribute missions, upon reaching the post station a vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture was dispatched to receive them with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever foreign states sent tribute envoys, upon reaching the post station a vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture was dispatched to receive them with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 明日至會同館，中書省奏聞，命禮部侍郎於館中禮待如儀。

translations.literal: The next day they went to the Hall of Joint Harmony; the Secretariat reported to the throne, and the vice minister of Rites was ordered to receive them at the hall according to protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they went to the Hall of Joint Harmony; the Secretariat reported to the throne, and the vice minister of Rites was ordered to receive them at the hall as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 宴畢，習儀三日，擇日朝見。

translations.literal: When the banquet was finished, they practiced the rites for three days, then a day was chosen for the audience.
translations.idiomatic: After the banquet they practiced the rites for three days, then a day was chosen for the audience.

sentences.zh: 陳設儀仗及進表，俱如儀。

translations.literal: Setting out the guard of honor and presenting the memorial were both as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: Setting out the guard of honor and presenting the memorial both followed the prescribed protocol.

sentences.zh: 承製官詣使者前，稱有制。

translations.literal: The edict-reciting officer went before the envoy and announced that there was an edict.
translations.idiomatic: The edict-reciting officer went before the envoy and announced that there was an edict.

sentences.zh: 使者跪，宣制曰：「皇帝問使者來時，爾國王安否？

translations.literal: The envoy knelt; the edict was proclaimed: "The emperor asks: when you set out, was your king's health well?
translations.idiomatic: The envoy knelt; the edict was proclaimed: "The emperor asks: when you set out, was your king in good health?

sentences.zh: 」使答畢，俯伏，興，再拜。

translations.literal: " When the envoy had answered, he prostrated himself, rose, and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " When the envoy had answered, he prostrated himself, rose, and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 承製官稱有後制，使者跪。

translations.literal: The edict-reciting officer announced there was a further edict; the envoy knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The edict-reciting officer announced there was a further edict; the envoy knelt.

sentences.zh: 宣制曰：「皇帝又問，爾使者遠來勤勞。

translations.literal: The edict was proclaimed: "The emperor further asks: you have come from afar in toil.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was proclaimed: "The emperor further asks: you have traveled far in toil.

sentences.zh: 」使者俯伏，興，再拜。

translations.literal: " The envoy prostrated himself, rose, and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy prostrated himself, rose, and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 承製官覆命訖，使者復四拜。

translations.literal: When the edict-reciting officer had reported completion, the envoy again performed four bows.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict-reciting officer had reported completion, the envoy again performed four bows.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，皇帝興，樂作止如儀。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, the emperor rose; music sounded and ceased as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete the emperor rose; music played and ceased as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 見東宮四拜，進方物訖，復四拜。

translations.literal: Four bows to the crown prince; when tribute objects were presented, four bows again.
translations.idiomatic: Four bows to the crown prince; after presenting tribute objects, four bows again.

sentences.zh: 謁丞相、大都督、御史大夫，再拜。

translations.literal: They paid court to the chancellor, regional commander-in-chief, and chief censor, bowing twice.
translations.idiomatic: They paid court to the chancellor, regional commander-in-chief, and chief censor, bowing twice.

sentences.zh: 獻書，復再拜。

translations.literal: They presented written works and again bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: They presented written works and again bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 見左司郎中等，皆鈞禮。

translations.literal: In meeting Left Department director-rank officials and the like, all followed the standard mutual rite.
translations.idiomatic: In meeting Left Department director-rank officials and the like, all followed the standard mutual rite.

sentences.zh: 凡錫宴，陳御座于謹身殿。

translations.literal: Whenever a banquet was bestowed, the imperial throne was set up in the Hall of Self-Cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a banquet was bestowed, the imperial throne was set up in the Hall of Self-Cultivation.

sentences.zh: 設皇太子座於御座東，諸王座於皇太子下，西向，設蕃王座於殿西第一行，東向，設文武官座於第二、第三行，東西向。

translations.literal: The crown prince's seat was set east of the imperial throne; princes' seats below the crown prince, facing west; the foreign king's seat in the first row on the west side of the hall, facing east; civil and military officials' seats in the second and third rows, facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's seat was set east of the imperial throne; princes' seats below him, facing west; the foreign king's seat in the first row on the west side of the hall, facing east; and civil and military officials' seats in the second and third rows, facing east and west.

sentences.zh: 酒九行，上食五次，大樂、細樂間作，呈舞隊。

translations.literal: Nine rounds of wine, five courses served, grand and fine music alternating, dance troupes presented.
translations.idiomatic: There were nine rounds of wine and five courses; grand and fine music alternated, and dance troupes were presented.

sentences.zh: 蕃國從官坐於西廡下，酒數食品同，不作樂。

translations.literal: Attendant officials of foreign states sat beneath the western gallery; wine rounds and food were the same, but no music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant officials of foreign states sat beneath the western gallery; the wine rounds and food were the same, but no music was performed.

sentences.zh: 東宮宴蕃王，殿上正中設皇太子座，設諸王座於旁，東西向；

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace banqueted the foreign king, the crown prince's seat was set at the center of the hall; princes' seats beside him, facing east and west;
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace banqueted the foreign king, the crown prince's seat was set at the center of the hall, with princes' seats beside him facing east and west;

sentences.zh: 蕃王座於西偏，諸王之下，東向；

translations.literal: the foreign king's seat on the western side, below the princes, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: the foreign king's seat on the western side, below the princes, facing east;

sentences.zh: 三師、賓客、諭德位於殿上第二行，東西向；

translations.literal: masters, guests of honor, and tutors in the second row on the hall platform, facing east and west;
translations.idiomatic: masters, guests of honor, and tutors in the second row on the hall platform, facing east and west;

sentences.zh: 蕃王從官及東宮官位於西廡，東向北上。

translations.literal: attendant officials of the foreign king and Eastern Palace officials at the western gallery, facing east toward the north.
translations.idiomatic: attendant officials of the foreign king and Eastern Palace officials at the western gallery, facing east toward the north.

sentences.zh: 和聲郎陳樂，光祿寺設酒饌，俱如謹身殿儀。

translations.literal: Harmonizers arrayed music; the Directorate of Imperial Entertainments set out wine and food—all as in the Hall of Self-Cultivation protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonizers arrayed music and the Directorate of Imperial Entertainments set out wine and food—all as in the Hall of Self-Cultivation protocol.

sentences.zh: 或宰相請旨宴勞，則設席於中書省後堂，賓西主東。

translations.literal: Or if the chancellor requested permission to banquet and comfort them, seats were set in the rear hall of the Secretariat, guest west and host east.
translations.idiomatic: Or if the chancellor requested permission to banquet and comfort them, seats were set in the Secretariat's rear hall, guest west and host east.

sentences.zh: 設蕃王從官及左右司官坐於左司。

translations.literal: Seats for the foreign king's attendants and Left and Right Department officials were set in the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: Seats for the foreign king's attendants and Left and Right Department officials were set in the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 教坊司陳樂於堂及左司南楹。

translations.literal: The Imperial Music Bureau arrayed music in the hall and on the southern eaves of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Music Bureau arrayed music in the hall and on the southern eaves of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 蕃王至省門外，省官迎入，從官各從其後。

translations.literal: When the foreign king reached outside the Secretariat gate, Secretariat officials welcomed him in; attendants each followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: When the foreign king reached outside the Secretariat gate, Secretariat officials welcomed him in; attendants each followed behind.

sentences.zh: 升階就坐，酒七行，食五品，作樂，雜陳諸戲。

translations.literal: Ascending the steps and taking seats; seven rounds of wine, five courses, music performed, various entertainments presented.
translations.idiomatic: They ascended the steps and took their seats; there were seven rounds of wine and five courses, with music and various entertainments.

sentences.zh: 宴畢，省官送至門外。

translations.literal: When the banquet was finished, Secretariat officials escorted him to outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet was finished, Secretariat officials escorted him to outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 都督府御史臺宴如之。

translations.literal: Banquets at the Regional Military Commission and Censorate followed the same protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Banquets at the Regional Military Commission and Censorate followed the same protocol.

sentences.zh: 其宴蕃使，禮部奉旨錫宴於會同館。

translations.literal: For banqueting foreign envoys, the Ministry of Rites, by imperial decree, bestowed a banquet at the Hall of Joint Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: For banqueting foreign envoys, the Ministry of Rites, by imperial decree, bestowed a banquet at the Hall of Joint Harmony.

sentences.zh: 館人設坐次及御酒案，教坊司設樂舞，禮部官陳龍亭於午門外。

translations.literal: The hall staff set seating order and the imperial wine table; the Imperial Music Bureau set music and dance; Ministry of Rites officials set up the dragon pavilion outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The hall staff set seating order and the imperial wine table; the Imperial Music Bureau set music and dance; and Ministry of Rites officers set up the dragon pavilion outside the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 光祿寺官請旨取御酒，置龍亭，儀仗鼓樂前導。

translations.literal: Directorate of Imperial Entertainments officials requested permission and took imperial wine, placed it in the dragon pavilion, with guard of honor and drums and music leading the way.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate of Imperial Entertainments officers requested permission, took imperial wine, placed it in the dragon pavilion, and led the way with guard of honor, drums, and music.

sentences.zh: 至館，蕃使出迎於門外。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the hall, the foreign envoy came out to welcome them outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the hall, the foreign envoy came out to welcome them outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 執事者捧酒由中道入，置酒於案。

translations.literal: Attendants bore the wine in along the central way and placed it on the table.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants bore the wine in along the central way and placed it on the table.

sentences.zh: 奉旨官立於案東，稱有制，使者望闕跪。

translations.literal: The edict-bearer official stood east of the table, announced there was an edict; the envoy faced the palace and knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The edict-bearer stood east of the table, announced there was an edict, and the envoy faced the palace and knelt.

sentences.zh: 聽宣畢，贊再拜。

translations.literal: When the proclamation was heard to completion, the herald called for a second bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation was heard to completion, the herald called for a second bow.

sentences.zh: 奉旨官酌酒授使者，北面跪飲畢，又再拜。

translations.literal: The edict-bearer official poured wine and handed it to the envoy; facing north he knelt, drank, finished, and again bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The edict-bearer poured wine and handed it to the envoy; facing north he knelt, drank, finished, and bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 各就坐，酒七行，湯五品，作樂陳戲如儀。

translations.literal: Each took his seat; seven rounds of wine, five courses of soup, music and entertainments as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: Each took his seat; there were seven rounds of wine and five courses of soup, with music and entertainments as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 宴畢，奉旨官出，使者送至門外。

translations.literal: When the banquet was finished, the edict-bearer official withdrew; the envoy escorted him to outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet was finished, the edict-bearer withdrew; the envoy escorted him to outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 皇太子錫宴，則遣宮官禮待之。

translations.literal: When the crown prince bestowed a banquet, palace officials were dispatched to receive them with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince bestowed a banquet, palace officials were dispatched to receive them with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 省府臺亦置酒宴會，酒五行，食五品，作樂，不陳戲。

translations.literal: The Secretariat, prefectural government, and Censorate also set out wine for banquets: five rounds of wine, five courses, music performed, but no entertainments presented.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat, prefectural government, and Censorate also held banquets with five rounds of wine and five courses, music performed, but no entertainments.

sentences.zh: ○遣使之蕃國儀

translations.literal: Protocol for dispatching envoys to foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys to foreign states.

sentences.zh: 凡遣使、賜璽綬及問遣慶弔，自漢始。

translations.literal: Dispatching envoys, bestowing seals and cords, and sending condolences and congratulations—all began in Han.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatching envoys, bestowing seals and cords, and sending condolences and congratulations all began in Han.

sentences.zh: 唐使外國，謂之入蕃使，宋謂之國信使。

translations.literal: Tang envoys to foreign states were called envoys entering the foreign lands; Song called them envoys of imperial trust.
translations.idiomatic: Tang envoys to foreign states were called envoys entering the foreign lands; Song called them envoys of imperial trust.

sentences.zh: 明祖既定天下，分遣使者奉詔書往諭諸國，或降香幣以祀其國之山川。

translations.literal: After the Ming founder had pacified the realm, he separately dispatched envoys bearing edicts to instruct the various states, or sent down incense and silks to sacrifice to the mountains and rivers of those states.
translations.idiomatic: After the Ming founder had pacified the realm, he separately dispatched envoys bearing edicts to instruct the various states, or sent down incense and silks to sacrifice to their mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 撫柔之意甚厚，而不傷國體，視前代爲得。

translations.literal: The intent to soothe and cherish was very generous, yet without harming dynastic dignity—regarded as better than previous dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The intent to soothe and cherish was very generous, yet without harming dynastic dignity—regarded as an improvement over previous dynasties.

sentences.zh: ，凡遣使，翰林院官草詔。

translations.literal: , Whenever envoys were dispatched, Hanlin Academy officials drafted the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever envoys were dispatched, Hanlin Academy officials drafted the edict.

sentences.zh: 至期，陳設如常儀。

translations.literal: When the day arrived, furnishings were set out as in the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: When the day arrived, furnishings were set out as in the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 百官入侍，皇帝御奉天殿。

translations.literal: The hundred officials entered attendance; the emperor took the Hall of Accepting Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials entered attendance; the emperor took the Hall of Accepting Heaven.

sentences.zh: 禮部官捧詔書，尚寶司奏用寶，以黃銷金袱裹置盤中，置於案。

translations.literal: Ministry of Rites officials bore the edict; the Office of Imperial Seals reported the use of the seal; it was wrapped in yellow gold-thread brocade, placed in a tray, and set on the table.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Rites officers bore the edict; the Office of Imperial Seals reported the use of the seal; it was wrapped in yellow gold-thread brocade, placed in a tray, and set on the table.

sentences.zh: 使者就拜位四拜，樂作止如儀。

translations.literal: The envoy took his bowing position and performed four bows; music sounded and ceased as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy took his bowing position and performed four bows; music played and ceased as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 承製官至丹陛稱有制，使者跪。

translations.literal: The edict-reciting officer reached the vermillion steps and announced there was an edict; the envoy knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The edict-reciting officer reached the vermillion steps and announced there was an edict; the envoy knelt.

sentences.zh: 宣制曰：「皇帝敕使爾某詔諭某國，爾宜恭承朕命。

translations.literal: The edict was proclaimed: "The emperor commands you, So-and-so, to bear an edict instructing such-and-such a state; you must respectfully receive Our command.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was proclaimed: "The emperor commands you, So-and-so, to bear an edict instructing such-and-such a state; you must respectfully receive Our command.

sentences.zh: 」宣訖，使者俯伏，興，四拜。

translations.literal: " When the proclamation was finished, the envoy prostrated himself, rose, and performed four bows.
translations.idiomatic: " When the proclamation was finished, the envoy prostrated himself, rose, and performed four bows.

sentences.zh: 禮部官奉詔降自中陛，以授使者。

translations.literal: Ministry of Rites officials bore the edict down the central steps and handed it to the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Rites officers bore the edict down the central steps and handed it to the envoy.

sentences.zh: 使者拜出午門，置龍亭內。

translations.literal: The envoy bowed and exited the Meridian Gate, placing it in the dragon pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy bowed and exited the Meridian Gate, placing the edict in the dragon pavilion.

sentences.zh: 駕興，百官出。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage rose; the hundred officials withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage rose; the hundred officials withdrew.

sentences.zh: 使者入蕃國境，先遣人報於王，王遣使遠接。

translations.literal: When the envoy entered foreign territory, he first sent someone to report to the king; the king dispatched envoys to welcome him from afar.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy entered foreign territory, he first sent someone to report to the king; the king dispatched envoys to welcome him from afar.

sentences.zh: 前期於國門外公館設幄結綵，陳龍亭香案，備金鼓儀仗大樂。

translations.literal: In advance, outside the national gate at the reception lodge, canopies were set up with colored hangings; a dragon pavilion and incense table were arrayed; gongs, drums, guard of honor, and grand music were prepared.
translations.idiomatic: In advance, outside the national gate at the reception lodge, canopies were set up with colored hangings; a dragon pavilion and incense table were arrayed; and gongs, drums, guard of honor, and grand music were prepared.

sentences.zh: 又於城內街巷結綵，設闕亭於王殿上，設香案於其前。

translations.literal: Within the city, streets and lanes were hung with colored festoons; a pavilioned gate was set on the king's hall; an incense table before it.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city, streets and lanes were hung with colored festoons; a pavilioned gate was set on the king's hall, with an incense table before it.

sentences.zh: 設捧詔官位殿陛之東北，宣詔展詔官以次南，俱西向。

translations.literal: The position for the edict-bearer was northeast of the hall steps; edict-proclaiming and edict-unfolding officials in order to the south, all facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The edict-bearer's station was northeast of the hall steps; edict-proclaiming and edict-unfolding officials stood in order to the south, all facing west.

sentences.zh: 詔使至，迎入館。

translations.literal: When the edict envoy arrived, he was welcomed into the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict envoy arrived, he was welcomed into the lodge.

sentences.zh: 王率國中官及耆老出迎於國門外，行五拜禮。

translations.literal: The king led the state's officials and elders to welcome outside the national gate, performing five bows.
translations.idiomatic: The king led the state's officials and elders to welcome outside the national gate, performing five bows.

sentences.zh: 儀仗鼓樂導龍亭入，使者隨之。

translations.literal: Guard of honor and drums and music led the dragon pavilion in; the envoy followed.
translations.idiomatic: Guard of honor, drums, and music led the dragon pavilion in; the envoy followed.

sentences.zh: 至殿上，置龍亭於正中。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the hall platform, the dragon pavilion was placed at the center.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the hall platform, the dragon pavilion was placed at the center.

sentences.zh: 使者立香案東，蕃王位殿庭中北向，衆官隨之。

translations.literal: The envoy stood east of the incense table; the foreign king at the center of the hall courtyard facing north; all officials followed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy stood east of the incense table; the foreign king at the center of the hall courtyard facing north; all officials followed.

sentences.zh: 使者南向立，稱有制，蕃王以下皆四拜。

translations.literal: The envoy stood facing south and announced there was an edict; the foreign king and all below performed four bows.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy stood facing south and announced there was an edict; the foreign king and all below performed four bows.

sentences.zh: 蕃王升自西階，詣香案前跪。

translations.literal: The foreign king ascended by the western steps and knelt before the incense table.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign king ascended by the western steps and knelt before the incense table.

sentences.zh: 三上香，俯伏，興，衆官同。

translations.literal: Thrice offering incense, he prostrated himself and rose—all officials likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Thrice offering incense, he prostrated himself and rose—all officials did likewise.

sentences.zh: 蕃王復位。

translations.literal: The foreign king returned to his position.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign king returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 使者詣龍亭前，取詔書授捧詔官。

translations.literal: The envoy went before the dragon pavilion and took the edict, handing it to the edict-bearer.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy went before the dragon pavilion, took the edict, and handed it to the edict-bearer.

sentences.zh: 捧詔官捧詣開讀案，授宣詔官。

translations.literal: The edict-bearer bore it to the edict-reading table and handed it to the edict-proclaiming officer.
translations.idiomatic: The edict-bearer bore it to the edict-reading table and handed it to the edict-proclaiming officer.

sentences.zh: 宣詔官受詔，展詔官對展，蕃王以下皆跪聽。

translations.literal: The proclaiming officer received the edict; the unfolding officer unfolded it facing him; the foreign king and all below knelt to listen.
translations.idiomatic: The proclaiming officer received the edict; the unfolding officer unfolded it facing him; the foreign king and all below knelt to listen.

sentences.zh: 宣訖，仍以詔置龍亭。

translations.literal: When the proclamation was finished, the edict was again placed in the dragon pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation was finished, the edict was again placed in the dragon pavilion.

sentences.zh: 蕃王以下皆俯伏，興，四拜，三舞蹈，復四拜。

translations.literal: The foreign king and all below prostrated themselves, rose, performed four bows, three dances, and again four bows.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign king and all below prostrated themselves, rose, performed four bows, three dances, and four more bows.

sentences.zh: 凡拜皆作樂。

translations.literal: Every bow was accompanied by music.
translations.idiomatic: Every bow was accompanied by music.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，使者以詔書付所司頒行。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, the envoy handed the edict to the relevant office for promulgation.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete, the envoy handed the edict to the relevant office for promulgation.

sentences.zh: 蕃王與使者分賓主行禮。

translations.literal: The foreign king and the envoy exchanged guest and host courtesies.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign king and the envoy exchanged guest and host courtesies.

sentences.zh: 其賜蕃王印綬及禮物，宣制曰：「皇帝敕使爾某，授某國王印綬，爾其恭承朕命。

translations.literal: When bestowing the seal cord on the foreign king, the edict proclaimed: "The emperor commands you, So-and-so, to confer upon the king of such-and-such a state the seal and cord; you must respectfully receive Our command.
translations.idiomatic: When bestowing the seal cord on the foreign king, the edict proclaimed: "The emperor commands you, So-and-so, to confer upon the king of such-and-such a state the seal and cord; you must respectfully receive Our command.

sentences.zh: 」至蕃國，宣制曰：「皇帝敕使某，持印賜爾國王某，並賜禮物。

translations.literal: " Upon reaching the foreign state, the edict proclaimed: "The emperor commands Envoy So-and-so to bear the seal and bestow it upon your king So-and-so, together with gifts.
translations.idiomatic: " Upon reaching the foreign state, the edict proclaimed: "The emperor commands Envoy So-and-so to bear the seal and bestow it upon your king So-and-so, together with gifts.

sentences.zh: 」餘如儀。

translations.literal: " The rest followed the prescribed protocol.
translations.idiomatic: " The rest followed the prescribed protocol.

sentences.zh: ○蕃國遣使進表儀

translations.literal: Protocol for foreign states dispatching envoys to present memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign envoys presenting memorials.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年定。

translations.literal: Fixed in the second year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed in Hongwu 2.

sentences.zh: 所司於王宮及國城街巷結綵，設闕庭於殿上正中。

translations.literal: The relevant offices hung colored festoons at the royal palace and throughout the streets and lanes of the capital; a pavilioned courtyard was set at the center of the hall platform.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices hung colored festoons at the royal palace and throughout the capital's streets and lanes; a pavilioned courtyard was set at the center of the hall platform.

sentences.zh: 前設表箋案，又前設香案。

translations.literal: Before it a memorial table was set, and before that an incense table.
translations.idiomatic: Before it a memorial table was set, and before that an incense table.

sentences.zh: 使者位於香案東，捧表箋二人於香案西。

translations.literal: The envoy stood east of the incense table; two officials bearing the memorial stood west of the incense table.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy stood east of the incense table; two officials bearing the memorial stood west of the incense table.

sentences.zh: 設龍亭於殿庭南正中，儀仗鼓樂具備。

translations.literal: A dragon pavilion was set at the due south center of the hall courtyard; guard of honor and drums and music were fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: A dragon pavilion was set at the due south center of the hall courtyard; guard of honor, drums, and music were fully prepared.

sentences.zh: 清晨，司印者陳印案於殿中，滌印訖，以表箋及印俱置於案。

translations.literal: At dawn, the seal keeper set out the seal desk in the hall; when the seal had been washed, both the memorial and formal letter and the seal were placed on the desk.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the seal keeper set out the seal desk in the hall; after washing the seal, he placed the memorial, formal letter, and seal together on the desk.

sentences.zh: 王冕服，衆官朝服。

translations.literal: The king in full ceremonial robes; the officials in court dress.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore full ceremonial robes; the officials wore court dress.

sentences.zh: 詣案前用印畢，用黃袱裹表，紅袱裹箋，各置於匣中，仍各以黃袱裹之。

translations.literal: Having gone before the desk and finished applying the seal, the memorial was wrapped in yellow cloth, the formal letter in red cloth, each placed in a case, and each again wrapped in yellow cloth.
translations.idiomatic: After going before the desk and applying the seal, they wrapped the memorial in yellow cloth and the formal letter in red, placed each in a case, and wrapped each case again in yellow cloth.

sentences.zh: 捧表箋官捧置於案。

translations.literal: The officials bearing the memorial and formal letter bore them and placed them on the desk.
translations.idiomatic: The officials bearing the memorial and formal letter placed them on the desk.

sentences.zh: 引禮引王至殿庭正中，衆官位其後。

translations.literal: A protocol guide led the king to the center of the hall courtyard; the officials took position behind him.
translations.idiomatic: A protocol guide led the king to the center of the hall courtyard, with the officials standing behind him.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，樂作。

translations.literal: An announcer called for bowing; music began.
translations.idiomatic: An announcer called for bowing; music began.

sentences.zh: 再拜，樂止。

translations.literal: They bowed twice; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed twice; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 王詣香案前跪，衆官皆跪，三上香訖。

translations.literal: The king went before the incense table and knelt; all officials knelt; three offerings of incense were completed.
translations.idiomatic: The king went before the incense table and knelt; all officials knelt and completed three offerings of incense.

sentences.zh: 捧表官取表東向跪進王，王授表以進於使者。

translations.literal: The memorial-bearer took the memorial, faced east, knelt, and presented it to the king; the king handed the memorial onward to the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial-bearer took the memorial, faced east, knelt, and presented it to the king, who handed it to the envoy.

sentences.zh: 使者西向跪受，興，置於案。

translations.literal: The envoy faced west, knelt to receive it, rose, and placed it on the desk.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy faced west, knelt to receive it, rose, and placed it on the desk.

sentences.zh: 贊興，王復位。

translations.literal: An announcer called to rise; the king returned to his position.
translations.idiomatic: An announcer called to rise; the king returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，樂作，王與衆官皆四拜。

translations.literal: An announcer called for bowing; music began; the king and all officials performed four bows.
translations.idiomatic: An announcer called for bowing; music began; the king and all officials performed four bows.

sentences.zh: 樂止，禮畢。

translations.literal: The music stopped; the rites were complete.
translations.idiomatic: The music stopped; the rites were complete.

sentences.zh: 捧表箋官捧表前行。

translations.literal: The officials bearing the memorial and formal letter bore the memorial and went forward.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial bearers took up the memorial and proceeded.

sentences.zh: 置於龍亭中，金鼓儀仗鼓樂前導。

translations.literal: They placed it in the dragon pavilion; gongs, drums, guard of honor, and music led in advance.
translations.idiomatic: They placed it in the dragon pavilion; gongs, drums, guard of honor, and music led the way.

sentences.zh: 王送至宮門外，還；

translations.literal: The king escorted them to outside the palace gate and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The king escorted them to beyond the palace gate and returned.

sentences.zh: 衆官朝服送至國門外。

translations.literal: The officials in court dress escorted them to outside the state gate.
translations.idiomatic: The officials in court dress escorted them to beyond the state gate.

sentences.zh: 使者乃行。

translations.literal: The envoy then set out.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy then set out.

sentences.zh: ○品官相見禮

translations.literal: Protocol for meetings between officials of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Meetings between officials of rank.

sentences.zh: 凡官員揖拜，洪武二十年定，公、侯、駙馬相見，各行兩拜禮。

translations.literal: For all bowing and salutation among officials: fixed in the twentieth year of Hongwu, when dukes, marquises, and imperial sons-in-law met one another, each performed the two-bow rite.
translations.idiomatic: As for bowing and salutation among officials: set in Hongwu 20, when dukes, marquises, and imperial sons-in-law met, each performed the two-bow rite.

sentences.zh: 一品官見公、侯、駙馬，一品官居右，行兩拜禮，公、侯、駙馬居左，答禮。

translations.literal: When a first-rank official met a duke, marquis, or imperial son-in-law, the first-rank official stood on the right and performed the two-bow rite; the duke, marquis, or imperial son-in-law stood on the left and returned the courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When a first-rank official met a duke, marquis, or imperial son-in-law, the first-rank official stood on the right and performed the two-bow rite; the duke, marquis, or imperial son-in-law stood on the left and returned the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 二品見一品亦如之。

translations.literal: Second rank meeting first rank was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank meeting first rank followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 三品以下仿此。

translations.literal: Third rank and below followed this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and below followed this pattern.

sentences.zh: 若三呂見一品，四品見二品，行兩拜禮。

translations.literal: If third rank met first rank, or fourth rank met second rank, they performed the two-bow rite.
translations.idiomatic: If third rank met first rank, or fourth rank met second rank, they performed the two-bow rite.

sentences.zh: 一品二品答受從宜，餘品仿此。

translations.literal: First and second rank returned the courtesy as appropriate; other ranks followed this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: First- and second-rank officials returned the courtesy as appropriate; other ranks followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 如有親戚尊卑之分，從行私禮。

translations.literal: If there was kinship with distinction of senior and junior, private rites were followed.
translations.idiomatic: Where kinship determined senior and junior standing, private rites took precedence.

sentences.zh: 三十年令，凡百官以品秩高下分尊卑。

translations.literal: An order of the thirtieth year: all officials distinguished senior from junior by rank and grade.
translations.idiomatic: An order of Hongwu 30: all officials distinguished senior from junior by rank and grade.

sentences.zh: 品近者行禮，則東西對立，卑者西，高者東。

translations.literal: When those close in rank exchanged courtesies, they stood facing east and west—the junior to the west, the senior to the east.
translations.idiomatic: When those close in rank exchanged courtesies, they stood facing east and west—the junior to the west, the senior to the east.

sentences.zh: 其品越二、三等者，卑者下，尊者上。

translations.literal: If ranks differed by two or three grades, the junior stood below, the senior above.
translations.idiomatic: If ranks differed by two or three grades, the junior stood below and the senior above.

sentences.zh: 其越四等者，則卑者拜下，尊者坐受，有事則跪白。

translations.literal: If they differed by four grades, the junior bowed from below, the senior sat to receive it; if there was business to report, the junior knelt and spoke.
translations.idiomatic: If they differed by four grades, the junior bowed from below while the senior sat to receive it; if there was business to report, the junior knelt and spoke.

sentences.zh: 凡文武官公聚，各依品級序坐。

translations.literal: Whenever civil and military officials gathered in public, each took a seat in order of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever civil and military officials gathered in public, each took a seat according to rank.

sentences.zh: 若資品同者，照衙門次第。

translations.literal: If credentials and rank were the same, order followed that of the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: If credentials and rank were equal, seating followed the order of the yamen.

sentences.zh: 若王府官與朝官坐立，各照品級，俱在朝官之次。

translations.literal: If princely establishment officials sat or stood with court officials, each followed rank, all placed after court officials.
translations.idiomatic: If princely establishment officials sat or stood with court officials, each followed rank, all placed after court officials.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年定，在外總兵、巡撫官位次，左右都督與左右都御史並，都督同知與副都御史並，都督僉事與僉都御史並，俱文東武西。

translations.literal: Fixed in Chenghua 14: the seating order for regional commanders and grand coordinators outside the capital—Left and Right Chief Commander paired with Left and Right Censor-in-Chief; Vice Commander with Vice Censor-in-Chief; Assistant Commander with Assistant Censor-in-Chief; all with civil east, military west.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed in Chenghua 14: outside the capital, regional commanders and grand coordinators were seated with Left and Right Chief Commander paired with Left and Right Censor-in-Chief, Vice Commander with Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Assistant Commander with Assistant Censor-in-Chief—civil officials to the east, military to the west.

sentences.zh: 伯以上則坐於左。

translations.literal: Barons and above sat on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Barons and above sat on the left.

sentences.zh: 十五年重定，都御史系總督及提督軍務者，不分左右副僉，俱坐於左。

translations.literal: Revised again in the fifteenth year: censors-in-chief who served as grand coordinators or directors of military affairs, without distinction of left, right, vice, or assistant, all sat on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Revised again in the fifteenth year: censors-in-chief serving as grand coordinators or directors of military affairs, whether left, right, vice, or assistant, all sat on the left.

sentences.zh: 總兵官雖伯，亦坐於右。

translations.literal: The regional commander, even if a baron, still sat on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commander, even if holding the rank of baron, still sat on the right.

sentences.zh: 凡官員相遇迴避，洪武三十年定，駙馬遇公侯，分路而行。

translations.literal: Whenever officials met and gave way: fixed in the thirtieth year of Hongwu, when an imperial son-in-law met a duke or marquis, they took separate roads.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever officials met and gave way: set in Hongwu 30, when an imperial son-in-law met a duke or marquis, they took separate roads.

sentences.zh: 一品、二品遇公、侯、駙馬，引馬側立，須其過。

translations.literal: First- and second-rank officials meeting dukes, marquises, or imperial sons-in-law reined in and stood aside, waiting for them to pass.
translations.idiomatic: First- and second-rank officials meeting dukes, marquises, or imperial sons-in-law reined in and stood aside until they had passed.

sentences.zh: 二品見一品，趨右讓道而行。

translations.literal: Second rank meeting first rank hastened to the right and yielded the road.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank meeting first rank hastened to the right and yielded the road.

sentences.zh: 三品遇公、侯、駙馬，引馬迴避，遇一品引馬側立，遇二品趨右讓道而行。

translations.literal: Third rank meeting dukes, marquises, or imperial sons-in-law reined aside; meeting first rank reined in and stood aside; meeting second rank hastened to the right and yielded the road.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank meeting dukes, marquises, or imperial sons-in-law reined aside; meeting first rank, reined in and stood aside; meeting second rank, hastened to the right and yielded the road.

sentences.zh: 四品遇一品以上官，引馬迴避，遇二品引馬側立，遇三品趨右讓道而行。

translations.literal: Fourth rank meeting officials of first rank or above reined aside; meeting second rank reined in and stood aside; meeting third rank hastened to the right and yielded the road.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank meeting officials of first rank or above reined aside; meeting second rank, reined in and stood aside; meeting third rank, hastened to the right and yielded the road.

sentences.zh: 五品至九品，皆視此遞差。

translations.literal: Fifth through ninth rank all followed this pattern in descending steps.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth through ninth rank all followed this pattern in descending steps.

sentences.zh: 其後盡遵行。

translations.literal: Thereafter all fully observed it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the rule was fully observed.

sentences.zh: 文職雖一命以上，不避公、侯、勳戚大臣；

translations.literal: Civil officials, though of ninth rank and above, did not give way to dukes, marquises, or meritorious kin among the great ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of ninth rank and above did not give way to dukes, marquises, or meritorious kin among the great ministers;

sentences.zh: 而其相迴避者，亦論官不論品秩矣。

translations.literal: Yet when they did give way to one another, office mattered, not rank and grade.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when they did give way to one another, it was office that mattered, not rank and grade.

sentences.zh: 凡屬官見上司，洪武二十年定，屬官序立於堂階之上，總行一揖，上司拱手，首領官答揖。

translations.literal: Whenever subordinate officials met their superior: fixed in the twentieth year of Hongwu, subordinates stood in order on the hall steps, all performed one salutation together; the superior cupped hands; the chief subordinate returned the salutation.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever subordinate officials met their superior: set in Hongwu 20, subordinates stood in order on the hall steps and performed one salutation together; the superior cupped his hands, and the chief subordinate returned the salutation.

sentences.zh: 其公幹節序見上司官，皆行兩拜禮，長官拱手，首領官答禮。

translations.literal: On seasonal occasions of official business when meeting the superior, all performed the two-bow rite; the chief official cupped hands; the chief subordinate returned the courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: On seasonal occasions of official business when meeting the superior, all performed the two-bow rite; the chief official cupped his hands, and the chief subordinate returned the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 凡官員公座，洪武二十年定，大小衙門官員，每日公座行肅揖禮。

translations.literal: Whenever officials held the public seating: fixed in the twentieth year of Hongwu, officials of yamens large and small performed the formal salutation rite at daily public seating.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever officials held public seating: set in Hongwu 20, officials of yamens large and small performed the formal salutation rite at daily public seating.

sentences.zh: 佐貳官揖長官，長官答禮。

translations.literal: Deputy officials saluted the chief; the chief returned the courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy officials saluted the chief; the chief returned the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 首領官揖長官、佐貳官，長官、佐貳官拱手。

translations.literal: Chief subordinates saluted the chief and deputies; the chief and deputies cupped hands.
translations.idiomatic: Chief subordinates saluted the chief and deputies; the chief and deputies cupped their hands.

sentences.zh: ○庶人相見禮

translations.literal: Protocol for meetings among commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Meetings among commoners.

sentences.zh: 洪武五年令，凡鄉黨序齒，民間士農工商人等平居相見及歲時宴會謁拜之禮，幼者先施。

translations.literal: An order of the fifth year of Hongwu: for all neighborhood ordering by age, the rites when scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants among the people met in daily life and at seasonal feasts and visits—the younger initiated the courtesy first.
translations.idiomatic: An order of Hongwu 5: in neighborhood ordering by age, when scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants met in daily life or at seasonal feasts and visits, the younger initiated the courtesy first.

sentences.zh: 坐次之列，長者居上。

translations.literal: In seating order, the elder held the upper place.
translations.idiomatic: In seating order, the elder held the upper place.

sentences.zh: 十二年令，內外官致仕居鄉，惟於宗族及外祖妻家序尊卑，如家人禮。

translations.literal: An order of the twelfth year: retired officials at home in the countryside ordered senior and junior only within clan and maternal grandfather's wife's family, as in family rites.
translations.idiomatic: An order of Hongwu 12: retired officials living in the countryside ordered senior and junior only within their clan and maternal grandfather's wife's family, as in family rites.

sentences.zh: 若筵宴，則設別席，不許坐於無官者之下。

translations.literal: At banquets a separate seat was set; they were not permitted to sit below those without official rank.
translations.idiomatic: At banquets a separate seat was provided; they were not to be seated below those without official rank.

sentences.zh: 與同致仕官會，則序爵；

translations.literal: When meeting fellow retired officials, they ordered by ennobled rank;
translations.idiomatic: When meeting fellow retired officials, they ordered themselves by ennobled rank;

sentences.zh: 爵同，序齒。

translations.literal: If ranks were equal, by age.
translations.idiomatic: if ranks were equal, by age.

sentences.zh: 其與異姓無官者相見，不須答禮。

translations.literal: When meeting unrelated persons without office, they need not return the courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When meeting unrelated persons without office, they need not return the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 庶民則以官禮謁見。

translations.literal: Commoners paid respects according to official rites when meeting them.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners paid respects according to official rites when meeting them.

sentences.zh: 凌侮者論如律。

translations.literal: Those who insulted them were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Those who insulted them were punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 二十六年定，凡民間子孫弟侄甥婿見尊長，生徒見其師，奴婢見家長，久別行四拜禮，近別行揖禮。

translations.literal: Fixed in the twenty-sixth year: whenever among the people sons, grandsons, younger brothers, nephews, and sons-in-law met elders; students met their teachers; servants met the household head—after long separation they performed the four-bow rite; after recent separation, the salutation rite.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed in Hongwu 26: among the people, when sons, grandsons, younger brothers, nephews, and sons-in-law met elders; when students met their teachers; when servants met the household head—after long separation they performed the four-bow rite; after recent separation, the salutation rite.

sentences.zh: 其餘親戚長幼悉依等第，久別行兩拜禮，近別行揖禮。

translations.literal: All other kinship by senior and junior followed their degrees—after long separation the two-bow rite; after recent separation, the salutation rite.
translations.idiomatic: All other kin by senior and junior standing followed their degrees—after long separation the two-bow rite; after recent separation, the salutation rite.

sentences.zh: 平交同。

translations.literal: Among equals, the same.
translations.idiomatic: Among equals, the same rule applied.
